Lâcher d’eau du barrage de Manantali : les populations invitées à la prudence
items.description: Il est donc demandé aux populations dont l'activité est liée à l'eau dans les zones environnantes du barrage de Manantali, à plus de prudence. Car, dans un communiqué publié mardi, la Société d'exploitation de Manantali et de Félou (Semaf), informe qu’elle procédera à des lâchers d'eau dans la semaine dès que le niveau du lac atteindra la cote 208,05 m IGN. La Société d'exploitation de Manantali et de Félou (Semaf) en charge de l'exploitation du barrage de Manantali, conformément aux consignes d'exploitation, informe les populations riveraines des cours d'eau en aval du barrage que la retenue de Manantali est proche de son niveau maximum d'exploitation. « En conséquence, elle procédera à des lâchers d'eau dans la semaine dès que le niveau du lac atteindra la cote 208,05 m IGN. Ces lâchers vont élever le niveau d'eau dans certaines zones riveraines du fleuve Sénégal. Il est donc demandé à tous ceux dont l'activité est liée à l'eau à plus de prudence dans les zones concernées », renseigne le texte. À cet effet, pour la protection des personnes et leurs biens, la Semaf appelle les populations riveraines du fleuve à prendre toutes les précautions utiles. L'arrêt des lâchers fera l'objet d'un communiqué ultérieur. Mariama DIEME

items.title: GoldBod recovers GH¢38.7m of GH¢55.8m outstanding receivables; remainder subject to legal action – Sammy Gyamfi
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi, has revealed that GoldBod has recovered GH¢38.7 million out of GH¢55.8 million in outstanding receivables, representing approximately 69 per cent of the total amount owed. He disclosed this when he appeared before Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. He said the remaining GH¢17.1 million was being pursued through legal proceedings, demand notices and negotiations with the parties concerned. He expressed hope that by the end of the year, 2026, GoldBod would have even increased what they have recovered. “Through demand notices, we have recovered a little over GH¢38.7 million, constituting about 69 percent of the amount. Of the remaining amount of GH¢17.1 million, GH¢7.5 million, approximately, relates to matters before courts of competent jurisdiction, and an amount of approximately GH¢9.6 million relates to debts that we are currently pursuing through various civil options like demand notices and negotiations with the parties concerned,” he said. Responding to questions about Red Sapphire, a private company appointed as an aggregator under the Bank of Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme, Mr Gyamfi said the company accounted for a significant portion of the outstanding receivables. He explained that the debt arose from assay fees payable on gold purchased by the company and submitted to GoldBod’s assayer for testing. “And per our records, gold that they bought and brought to our assayer, which we assayed, they are supposed to pay the amount you see before them, being assay fees. But their counter-argument is that that money is supposed to be paid by the Bank of Ghana to us. So we are currently negotiating with them and the Bank of Ghana to see who bears the liability, so that we can recover that amount.” Mr Gyamfi disclosed that GoldBod had recovered GH¢13.53 million from Red Sapphire, which had an outstanding debt of approximately GH¢16.14 million. The remaining balance is approximately GH¢2.61 million. The GoldBod CEO assured the committee that the board would continue pursuing the remaining receivables, with the aim of increasing the recovery rate before the end of 2026.

items.title: Kankan : le prix du gaz domestique flambe, de 60 000 à 125 000 GNF
items.description: Le prix de la recharge de gaz domestique a doublé à Kankan, provoquant l'inquiétude et la colère des ménages. D'environ 60 000 francs guinéens, le tarif est passé à 120 000 voire 125 000 GNF selon les points de vente. Une hausse constatée ce lundi par de nombreux usagers venus recharger leurs bouteilles. « D'habitude, on le fait à 60 000, mais aujourd'hui, quand je suis venue, on me dit que c'est à 125 000. C'est très inquiétant », déplore Fatoumata Diawara, veuve et mère de famille rencontrée sur place. Pour elle, le gaz était devenu une alternative au charbon, dont le sac se négocie désormais à 80 000 GNF sans tenir une semaine. « Tout le monde ne pourra pas avoir ces 120 000 francs. Même moi qui parle là, mon mari est décédé et j'ai des enfants à nourrir », confie-t-elle. Même constat chez Diakité Mouctar, qui affirme que la recharge des grosses bouteilles est passée de 130 000 à 250 000 GNF. « Vraiment, je veux que le gouvernement voie cela, sinon ce n'est pas bon pour nous, les citoyens », lance-t-il. Une autre consommatrice, Saran Doumbouya, dit avoir laissé sa bouteille trois semaines avant de découvrir la nouvelle tarification. « Cela fait trois semaines que ma bouteille est là. Je suis venue aujourd'hui la prendre et on me dit que ce n'est plus à 60 000, mais maintenant à 125 000 », raconte-t-elle. Elle précise avoir constaté un prix de 120 000 GNF à l'usine, contre 125 000 GNF dans les points de recharge des quartiers. Pour ces femmes qui doivent préparer rapidement les repas avant le marché, le gaz est devenu indispensable. « Ce que je peux dire au gouvernement, c'est de nous aider à diminuer le prix et d'avoir pitié de nous, les femmes », plaide Saran Doumbouya, qui interpelle directement le président Mamadi Doumbouya. Sollicité pour expliquer les raisons de cette flambée, le responsable du service de remplissage de gaz de Kankan a refusé de s'exprimer, affirmant ne pas avoir reçu l'autorisation de sa hiérarchie. En l'absence d'explications officielles, les consommateurs disent redouter une aggravation de la précarité énergétique. Entre charbon et gaz devenus inaccessibles, ils appellent les autorités à intervenir pour réguler les prix et soulager des budgets familiaux déjà fragilisés. Karifa Kansan Doumbouya, correspondant régional – Kankan L’article Kankan : le prix du gaz domestique flambe, de 60 000 à 125 000 GNF est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Tinubu writes Senate, seeks approval for N100.5bn Damaturu airport reimbursement
items.description: By Henry Umoru President Bola Tinubu has written the Senate, seeking approval of a N100.5 billion promissory note programme to reimburse the Yobe State Government for the cost of the Muhammadu Buhari International Cargo Airport in Damaturu. With the request, the Senate has been urged to consider a request for approval of the 70th Promissory Notes Programme for the reimbursement of the Yobe State Government for the takeover of the Muhammadu Buhari International Cargo Airport in Damaturu. In a letter addressed to the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, Tinubu, who sought legislative approval for the establishment and issuance of the promissory note programme through the Debt Management Office (DMO), said that the Federal Executive Council (FEC), at its second extraordinary meeting held on May 23, 2023, approved the takeover of the airport, constructed by the Yobe State Government, and the reimbursement of the project cost through a promissory note programme. According to the letter read on Tuesday by the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP) has completed its review of the project and recommended N100,509,017,234.55 for reimbursement to the state government. Tinubu said, “In the light of the foregoing, I urge the Senate to consider and approve the establishment and issuance by the Debt Management Office of a promissory note programme in the sum of N100,509,017,234.55.” The President also appealed to the lawmakers to expedite consideration of the request. “While looking forward to the expeditious action on this submission, please accept, Distinguished Senate President, the assurances of my highest esteem,” the letter read. The request was subsequently referred to the relevant Senate committee for further legislative consideration. If approved, the proposed programme would provide a mechanism for the Federal Government to reimburse Yobe State for the airport project, in line with the arrangement approved by the Federal Executive Council. The Senate’s decision will determine the next step in the proposed reimbursement process. The request was referred to the Senate Committee on Local and Foreign Debts, with a directive to report back to the Senate within one month. The post Tinubu writes Senate, seeks approval for N100.5bn Damaturu airport reimbursement appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: GEXIM Bank donates GH¢200,000 worth of medical equipment to Korle-Bu Child Health Department
items.description: The Head of Sustainability and Strategic Impact at the Ghana Export-Import Bank (GEXIM), Dr Abena Nyarkoa Asomaning, has presented medical equipment and supplies worth approximately GH¢200,000 to the Department of Child Health at the Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital to support the treatment of children. The donation, made on Tuesday, October 13, forms part of activities marking the bank’s 10th anniversary and its corporate social responsibility efforts to support institutions in need. The items, comprising more than 15 pieces of equipment and supplies, include patient monitors, defibrillators, an examination table, an oxygen cylinder, an emergency stretcher and other essential medical items. Presenting the items on behalf of GEXIM, Dr Asomaning said the intervention was intended to address some of the department’s immediate needs and contribute to improving healthcare delivery for children. She explained that although the bank’s core mandate was to support Ghana’s import and export activities, it also recognised the importance of contributing to national development through social interventions. Dr Asomaning said the bank had assessed requests from various institutions as part of its anniversary activities before selecting the Department of Child Health for support. She acknowledged that the donation would not address all the department’s challenges but described it as a first step towards building a lasting relationship with the hospital. She added that the bank’s engagement with the hospital would help it better understand the department’s challenges and identify areas where further assistance could be provided. “We will definitely come back. It’s the start of a relationship. We will definitely come back to support,” she said. Hospital welcomes support The Principal Nursing Officer at the Department of Child Health, Lawrencia Akweley Turkson, expressed gratitude to GEXIM, describing the donation as timely and beneficial to both patients and healthcare professionals. She said the equipment would provide staff with essential tools to carry out their duties and support the care of children receiving treatment at the facility. Ms Turkson noted that the department served patients from across Ghana and other parts of West Africa, making support for its operations particularly important. “We are so happy they came. Of all the hospitals in Ghana, we chose Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital, Department of Child Health. And I believe that is the best decision and the best choice because Korle-Bu receives patients from everywhere across Ghana, everywhere across West Africa,” she said. She said the donation was especially meaningful because it provided practical medical equipment, rather than consumables that the department often received from donors. “Initially, when we are receiving donations, we normally receive drinks, juice and other things. But, I mean, this is so touching; we have medical equipment to work with. And it helps the patients; it helps the staff as well,” she said. Ms Turkson urged other corporate organisations to support the department and appealed to the public to contribute to its ‘100 by 100’ initiative, launched in July to raise funds for needy patients, medical equipment and infrastructure. The initiative aims to mobilise 100,000 people to donate at least GH¢100 each towards improving the department’s capacity to provide care. She expressed confidence that the target could be achieved through collective support and encouraged the public to participate.

items.title: Atteinte à la laïcité : Un créateur de contenu et ses acolytes interpellés au Burkina Faso
items.description: Plusieurs personnes, dont des femmes et des hommes, ont été interpellées à la suite de la diffusion sur les réseaux sociaux d’une vidéo dans laquelle un homme identifié comme créateur de contenus affirme, en langue nationale mooré, vouloir voir les mosquées et les églises quitter le Burkina Faso. Dans cette séquence, l’intervenant évoque également la promotion de pratiques traditionnelles dans des lieux de culte musulmans et chrétiens, avant de conclure son discours par une menace de mort. Selon les informations parvenues à Faso7 ce 13 octobre 2026, les individus apparaissant dans cette vidéo ont été appréhendés par les autorités compétentes. Dans la vidéo, le principal intervenant ne cache pas ses intentions. « Nous avons dit que les mosquées et les églises vont quitter le Burkina Faso. Ce n’est pas de la négociation » , déclare-t-il devant plusieurs personnes présentes à ses côtés. Il présente cette position comme un engagement qu’il entend maintenir. Pour justifier son discours, il propose notamment de se rendre à La Mecque et à Médine afin d’y installer des lieux dédiés aux pratiques traditionnelles et de convaincre les musulmans d’abandonner l’islam. Il développe un raisonnement similaire à propos de Jérusalem et de Bethléem, où il souhaite voir les chrétiens renoncer à leur foi au profit de ces mêmes pratiques. La séquence, qui prend ainsi des allures de défi lancé aux deux religions, se termine par une formule qui détourne la devise du Burkina Faso : « La Patrie ou la Mort Nous Vaincrons ! Mais s’ils ne nous aiment pas ? Vous mourrez alors ». Les personnes visées par cette menace ne sont pas clairement identifiées dans la vidéo. Les personnes interpellées pourraient être poursuivies conformément aux dispositions légales en vigueur au Burkina Faso, notamment celles relatives à la laïcité. La liberté religieuse n’autorise pas tout Le Burkina Faso dispose désormais de la loi n°020-2026/ALP du 20 juin 2026 relative aux libertés religieuses. Ce texte prévoit des sanctions pénales contre les discours haineux fondés sur la croyance religieuse, l’incitation à de tels discours et les propos visant à dénigrer ou à discréditer une religion, ses doctrines ou ses fidèles. L’article 88 prévoit une peine d’emprisonnement d’un à cinq ans et une amende de 2 à 5 millions de francs CFA pour quiconque profère un discours haineux dirigé contre une personne ou un groupe de personnes sur la base de la croyance religieuse. L’article 89 prévoit trois à sept ans d’emprisonnement et une amende de 5 à 10 millions de francs CFA pour l’incitation à la profération d’un discours haineux. Quant à l’article 91, il prévoit un à cinq ans d’emprisonnement et une amende de 2 à 5 millions de francs CFA pour les propos visant à dénigrer, outrager ou discréditer une religion, un courant religieux, ses doctrines ou ses fidèles. Les dispositions applicables aux personnes interpellées et les suites judiciaires éventuelles devront être appréciées au regard des faits retenus par les autorités compétentes. En attendant, cette affaire rappelle que les réseaux sociaux ne soustraient pas leurs utilisateurs aux règles encadrant les libertés religieuses. Au Burkina Faso, où la coexistence entre les communautés musulmanes, chrétiennes et adeptes des religions traditionnelles constitue un enjeu de cohésion sociale, les provocations visant les croyances d’autrui peuvent rapidement dépasser le cadre d’une simple querelle en ligne. Josué TIENDREBEOGO Faso7 L’article Atteinte à la laïcité : Un créateur de contenu et ses acolytes interpellés au Burkina Faso est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

RDC : L’ancien président Joseph Kabila entre en rébellion contre le pouvoir Tshisekedi
items.description: L’ancien président de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC), Joseph Kabila, a pris la tête d’un nouveau mouvement politico-militaire dénommé Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN). La création de cette structure, annoncée le lundi 12 octobre 2026 à Goma, dans l’est du pays, marque une nouvelle étape dans l’opposition armée au régime du président Félix Tshisekedi. Selon une déclaration politique rendue publique à Goma, le FRN entend fédérer et coordonner les forces opposées au pouvoir de Kinshasa. Le document prévoit le recours à tous les moyens, y compris la force, pour mettre fin à ce que les signataires qualifient de « tyrannie ». Le nouveau mouvement succède à l’Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC), dont la dissolution est annoncée dans le document constitutif. L’AFC était associée au Mouvement du 23 mars (M23), un groupe rebelle qui contrôle plusieurs zones dans l’est de la RDC. Joseph Kabila a été désigné président du FRN. Corneille Nangaa et Bertrand Bisimwa figurent parmi les responsables de la nouvelle coalition, tandis que Sultani Makenga, chef militaire du M23, est présenté comme chef d’état-major général de l’Armée révolutionnaire congolaise (ARC). Cette annonce intervient dans un contexte de conflit persistant dans l’est de la RDC et de négociations visant à parvenir à une solution politique. Elle intervient également alors que Joseph Kabila multiplie les critiques contre la gouvernance de son successeur, Félix Tshisekedi. À ce stade, les autorités congolaises n’avaient pas encore officiellement réagi à l’annonce de la création du FRN, selon les informations disponibles le 13 octobre 2026. Minute.bf

items.title: Majority rejects Minority’s claims over GH¢49.7m South Africa evacuation, calls for forensic probe
items.description: The Majority on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration Committee has rejected the Minority’s allegation that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has failed to account for GH¢49.7 million spent on the evacuation of Ghanaians from South Africa. The caucus described the claims as “dubious political mischief”. Chairman of the Committee, Dr Alfred Okoe Vanderpuije, dismissed the Minority’s allegations, insisting that the Ministry had accounted for the expenditure. He said a document spanning more than 200 pages, submitted in response to the Minority’s request under the Right to Information (RTI) law, provides details of the expenditure incurred during the evacuation exercise. Dr Vanderpuije maintained that the records presented by the Ministry contradict the Minority’s claims of non-accountability. The Majority is instead calling on the Attorney-General to initiate a forensic investigation into all evacuation exercises undertaken by the erstwhile New Patriotic Party (NPP) government. The Minority has insisted that the Ministry must provide a full account of the funds, while the Majority maintains that the documents submitted adequately address the concerns raised.

items.title: Engineers urge Tinubu to halt Lagos-Calabar highway diversion
items.description: Iwere Engineers Forum, IEF, has urged President Bola Tinubu to immediately intervene in the reported plan to divert some sections of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway away from the Atlantic coastline as the route approaches major Ilaje communities and the Itsekiri coastal belt. IEF said the engineering concerns cited by the Ministry of Works in the Ondo and Delta corridors, including deep peat, weak soils and large water crossings, were not sufficient justification for abandoning the areas. In a statement, the forum’s Chairman of the Board of Trustees, Professor Ogbemi Omatete; Vice Chairman, Gbesimi Akperi; General Secretary, Dr Silver Ejejigbe; and members Kunu Harmony, Dr Felix U. Atakere and Jude Pemu, said modern engineering offered multiple solutions, including corridor optimisation, strategic setbacks from the active shoreline, pile-supported embankments, viaducts, long-span bridges, staged consolidation, vertical drains, lightweight fills, deep foundations, advanced geotechnical monitoring and climate-resilient drainage. They urged the President to direct an immediate, independent comparative review of the Ondo-Delta alignment and make relevant alignment drawings, chainages, geotechnical assessments, bridge assumptions and comparative life-cycle cost evidence available to affected stakeholders, subject to legitimate security and procurement restrictions. They also called for the establishment of a joint technical working group involving the Federal Ministry of Works, relevant environmental and maritime agencies, the Ondo and Delta state governments, qualified independent engineers, including IEF, and representatives of affected coastal communities. The statement reads: “Our position is straightforward: a national project conceived, named and justified as a Coastal Highway should, subject to sound engineering and environmental safeguards, remain functionally coastal. It should run broadly parallel to the Atlantic coastline and directly unlock the coastal settlements, ports, jetties, fisheries, industrial locations and blue-economy assets for which such a corridor is uniquely valuable. Inland cities and state capitals can and should be connected to the trunk coastal corridor by high-quality strategic spurs and interchanges. The trunk road itself should not have to abandon the coastal development belt merely to provide access that can be achieved through connectors. “We acknowledge that the Federal Ministry of Works has publicly cited serious engineering concerns in the Ondo and Delta corridors, including deep peat, weak soils and large water crossings. IEF does not dismiss those concerns. Our concern is that they should not become reasons to abandon the coastal development objective before a transparent, independently verifiable comparison of viable set-back and hybrid coastal alignments has been completed. Modern engineering provides multiple responses: corridor optimisation, strategic setbacks from the active shoreline, pile-supported embankments, viaducts, long-span bridges, staged consolidation, vertical drains, lightweight fills, deep foundations, advanced geotechnical monitoring and climate-resilient drainage. “The appropriate engineering question is therefore not whether the road must sit on the beach. It should not. The question is whether a resilient Atlantic-facing corridor, generally set back from the active shoreline and locally adjusted around exceptional geotechnical, ecological and navigational constraints, can maintain direct access to the Ilaje and Itsekiri coastal belt. We submit that this alternative deserves full feasibility-level investigation before the coastal corridor is foreclosed. “The coastal road idea in this axis has deep historical roots. Public historical accounts of the late Chief Festus Okotie-Eboh record the planning of the Koko-Ogheye motor road, while later accounts describe the Koko-Ogheye-Epe concept as a coastal connection intended to shorten travel between Lagos and the Niger Delta. The Koko port facilities, Escravos navigation and other maritime infrastructure formed part of the same broader development vision. We therefore respectfully urge that today’s Lagos-Calabar project preserve, rather than bypass, the strategic maritime logic of connecting the Atlantic economic belt. “Coastal and deltaic highways are difficult infrastructure projects, but they are not unprecedented. Louisiana’s Department of Transportation and Development, for example, is replacing a vulnerable portion of LA 1 through sensitive coastal wetlands with an approximately 18-mile elevated highway because the existing route is affected by subsidence, erosion and flooding. The lesson is not that Nigeria should copy another country blindly; it is that modern highway engineering can maintain critical coastal access through weak wetland environments where the strategic case justifies the investment. Nigeria should subject the Ilaje-Itsekiri alternatives to the same disciplined engineering test. “There is also a relevant Nigerian precedent within the same Niger Delta coastal environment. The Chevron Escravos Terminal is served by an established asphalt runway in the Escravos coastal belt, constructed and operated on low-lying deltaic terrain and used for regular personnel and logistics flights, including aircraft in approximately the 100-passenger class. Its long-standing operation demonstrates that major transport infrastructure can be engineered and maintained in this difficult coastal setting. IEF therefore recommends that the comparative study obtain and review available geotechnical, pavement, ground-improvement, drainage and maintenance records for the Escravos runway as a Nigerian benchmark. The precise equivalence of its soil strata to those at any proposed highway chainage should, of course, be confirmed through site-specific geotechnical investigations. “The weak-soil argument must also be considered in its wider Niger Delta context. Soft, compressible clay, organic deposits, peat, high groundwater levels and swamp conditions are not unique to the Ilaje-Itsekiri axis; similarly difficult foundation conditions occur extensively across the Bayelsa and Rivers coastal and deltaic belts, through which a genuinely coastal Lagos-Calabar corridor must ultimately pass. Diverting substantially inland whenever weak coastal soil is encountered would progressively convert the project from an Atlantic coastal highway into an inland highway. It could also increase travel distances and times between Lagos and the South-South coastal economic belt. The engineering objective should therefore be to optimise the coastal alignment and apply appropriate ground-improvement, piled, elevated or hybrid solutions where justified, rather than treating difficult but regionally characteristic terrain as an automatic reason to abandon the coast. “Importantly, the coastal engineering geology and geotechnical challenges are regionally comparable from Ondo through Delta, Bayelsa and Rivers to the Cross River coastal belt. Although site-specific soil conditions vary and must be verified through boreholes and surveys, the same reasoning used to divert the highway inland in Ondo could repeatedly push it inland through Bayelsa, Rivers and ultimately Cross River State. Such successive diversions would progressively undermine the intended Atlantic and coastal function and could increase travel distances between Lagos and the South-South rather than provide the most direct coastal connection. “Modern highway and bridge engineering provides alternative methods for transferring structural loads through weak soils, reducing embankment settlement and maintaining road elevations above flood levels. The engineering question should therefore not be whether a highway can be constructed through such terrain, but rather: Which foundation and superstructure system provides the best combination of safety, constructability, environmental protection, whole-life cost and long-term reliability? “Many communities along this coast face chronic erosion, flooding and shoreline retreat. The highway programme offers a once-in-a-generation opportunity to combine transportation access with a coordinated coastal-resilience programme. The scope should therefore include shoreline-risk mapping, beach and dune management where appropriate, revetments or other protective structures only where coastal-process modelling supports them, drainage and flood-resilience works, and permanent access routes capable of transporting rock, armour units, piling equipment and emergency materials to threatened coastlines. Road access can dramatically improve the logistics of constructing and maintaining shoreline protection. “A true Atlantic corridor can connect coastal industrial zones, jetties, fisheries, marine logistics bases, fabrication facilities, energy infrastructure and future ports to the national road network. It can reduce the cost of moving heavy equipment and manufactured goods between inland markets and coastal loading and offloading points. Properly planned interchanges can create new industrial clusters without forcing heavy traffic through traditional settlements. “The corridor can support fisheries, aquaculture, cold-chain logistics, marine services, tourism, ports, offshore energy support, ship repair, coastal manufacturing and other blue-economy activities. These benefits should be quantified through a formal socioeconomic and transport-economic study, but excluding coastal communities from direct road access risks leaving precisely the maritime economy that a coastal highway could unlock outside the project’s main development corridor. “Direct road access can materially improve the speed and reliability of police, civil defence, fire, ambulance, disaster-response and maritime-security operations in isolated coastal settlements. A continuous coastal corridor would also provide evacuation and relief-distribution capacity during flooding and other emergencies. Communications ducts, fibre, power infrastructure and emergency lay-bys could be integrated into the right-of-way, strengthening both civilian resilience and legitimate security operations. “Road and fibre connectivity can reduce the isolation of coastal schools, health centres and communities; improve access to universities and technical training; make it easier for teachers, doctors and skilled personnel to serve the region; and allow digital services and telecommunications infrastructure to reach communities that are currently expensive to connect. Better mobility can also make participation in lawful civic, administrative and political processes easier by reducing geographic isolation. “Construction and long-term operation can create opportunities in civil works, marine logistics, surveying, maintenance, hospitality, fisheries logistics, fabrication, security support and other services. This should be accompanied by transparent local-content programmes, skills certification and apprenticeships so that host communities participate not merely as observers but as trained contributors to the infrastructure economy. “IEF strongly supports the development of Edo State, inland Ondo and inland Delta. This need not be an either-or proposition. Strategic spurs can connect Igbokoda and other Ondo centres, Edo economic nodes, Warri, Koko and other inland locations to the coastal trunk road. A hierarchy of a trunk highway and connecting spurs can deliver both coastal transformation and inland accessibility without sacrificing the defining coastal function of the Lagos-Calabar project. “The Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway has the potential to become one of the defining infrastructure legacies of this administration. That legacy will be strongest if future generations can see a continuous national Atlantic development corridor that opens previously isolated coastal communities to commerce, security, education, healthcare, communications and industry while protecting vulnerable shorelines. A road that runs substantially inland across a major coastal region may still be a valuable highway, but it would not deliver the same coastal-development benefits to the communities it bypasses.” The post Engineers urge Tinubu to halt Lagos-Calabar highway diversion appeared first on Vanguard News .

APGA hails Soludo’s inclusion in APC presidential campaign council
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The ruling All Progressives Grand Alliance, APGA, in Anambra State has hailed Governor Chukwuma Soludo’s inclusion as a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu, describing it as a recognition of his leadership qualities. Governor Soludo’s APGA is not presenting a presidential candidate in 2027 and the party is fully supporting the APC presidential candidate, President Bola Tinubu, for the election. National Publicity Secretary of APGA, Dr. Ejimofor Opara, in a statement, said the governor’s appointment is a recognition of his commitment to progressive ideals. According to Opara, the appointment reflects Soludo’s advocacy for strategic cooperation between APGA and the federal government for the benefit of Anambra State and the South East geopolitical zone. Opara’s statement read: “The National Working Committee (NWC) of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) heartily congratulates our national leader and Governor of Anambra State, Prof. Chukwuma Charles Soludo, on his well-deserved appointment as the Anambra State Coordinator of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu 2027 Presidential Campaign Council. “This appointment is a testament to Governor Soludo’s exemplary leadership, his uncommon commitment to progressive ideals, and his consistent advocacy for a strategic partnership between APGA and the Federal Government for the collective good of Ndi Anambra and Ndigbo at large. “As a party, APGA has made its position clear. At our National Executive Committee meeting and during Mr. President’s working visit to Anambra on May 8, 2025, we formally adopted President Bola Ahmed Tinubu as our consensus presidential candidate for the 2027 general election. In line with this resolution, APGA did not field a presidential candidate for the 2027 election. “Governor Soludo’s mantra that ‘Progressives are Working Together’ is not just a slogan, but a statement of historical truth. APGA, as the first truly progressive party in Nigeria, shares ideological DNA with the progressive movement at the centre. “This synergy has already yielded tangible dividends for Anambra State, including federal collaboration on critical infrastructural interventions and economic development enablers. “While APGA remains firmly in control of Anambra State, our position remains that in Anambra, it is Tinubu for President, APGA for Senate, House of Representatives, and State House of Assembly.” He said the party’s decision not to field a presidential candidate in 2027 is consistent with its earlier resolution to support Tinubu, adding that the political alignment with the ruling APC was rooted in the shared progressive ideals that had facilitated federal collaboration on infrastructure and economic development in Anambra State. He expressed confidence that Soludo’s intellectual capacity, organisational skills and political influence across the South East would help mobilise support for Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda ahead of the 2027 elections. The post APGA hails Soludo’s inclusion in APC presidential campaign council appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: GEXIM urges banks to support refurbishment of Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital’s Child Health Department
items.description: The Ghana Export-Import Bank (GEXIM) has called on financial institutions to support the refurbishment of the Child Health Department of the Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital to improve care for children, particularly those battling childhood cancers. Deputy Head of Legal at GEXIM and President of the bank’s Ladies Association, Emma Nancy Mullen, made the appeal during an interview with journalists after the bank donated medical equipment and supplies worth an estimated GH¢200,000 to the hospital on Tuesday, October 13, as part of its 10th anniversary celebrations. She said the visit had exposed significant infrastructure needs at the department, adding that the bank would engage hospital management to explore further support. “The whole building needs refurbishment and renovation, so we would come back, we would engage Korle-Bu to see what we can do,” she said. Ms Mullen urged other banks to join the effort, noting that the hospital receives referrals from across Ghana and other parts of West Africa. “When we all come on board as a bank, with other banks, we can do well to develop this centre into a first-class healthcare provider,” she added. The donation, which includes patient monitors, defibrillators, an examination table, an oxygen cylinder and an emergency stretcher, forms part of GEXIM’s corporate social responsibility efforts. Deputy Manager of Corporate Banking and President of the bank’s Men’s Association, Papa Kwadwo Abebrese, said the items were selected after assessing requests from health institutions. He said the donation was intended to address some of the unit’s immediate needs, although more support would be required. “We know it’s not enough, but at least a start is better than nothing,” he said. The bank says its anniversary initiative reflects its commitment to supporting communities beyond its core mandate of financing export businesses.

items.title: Man kills wife over land sale, commits suicide in Delta
items.description: By Akpokona Omafuaire, UGHELLI TRAGEDY struck in Agbarho Community of Ughelli North Local Government Area, Delta State, as an aggrieved man dismembered his wife, and then committed suicide by drinking poisonous substance. Read Also: Atiku’s aide challenges Wike to publish invoices for media chats They leave behind four children. A source told Vanguard that the aggrieved man reacted angrily to his wife’s alleged infidelity and sale of his landed property. A neighbour at Owiri street, Agbarho, where the incident occurred, said that the deceased couple had been having a series of physical confrontations. Also, an elder brother of the diseased man expressed sadness over the incident. He told Vanguard that he didn’t know much about what brought about the fight. But said that as family, there are different situations that could cause a confrontation. He narrated that his late brother had four children with the eldest son about 21years old. He, however, refused to disclosed his name, and that of his late couple. Calls for confirmation to the Delta State Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bright Edafe, were not successful at press time. However, a senior police officer at Agbarho Division, who pleaded anonymity, confirmed the incident. He said the police evacuated both corpses to the morgue for further investigation, after being informed of the calamity. He further said that no official complaint has been made either by families of the diseased. items.title: Joj Dakar 2026 : petite balle, grandes ambitions
items.description: Méconnue du grand public sénégalais, la discipline du tennis de table s’apprête à profiter de la vitrine des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026. Entre stages à l’étranger, entraînements intensifs et ambitions internationales, les pongistes sénégalais peaufinent leur préparation. Il est 11 h 30, ce samedi. Le ciel couvert de Dakar annonce les pluies prévues pour le week-end. Aux abords du stade Léopold-Sédar-Senghor, les flaques d’eau boueuse compliquent l’accès aux installations. Pour éviter de s’y mouiller les pieds, il faut parfois improviser quelques sauts. Une pierre, à peine visible au milieu de l’eau, sert de point d’appui aux visiteurs les plus téméraires. Une fois le portail franchi, il faut longer l’extérieur du stade et chercher la bonne entrée. « Il y a une porte entre les entrées 15 et 16 », indique un interlocuteur dont le numéro figure sur la page de la Fédération sénégalaise de tennis de table. Après quelques détours, des sons secs et répétitifs attirent l’attention. Une petite balle percute une raquette, rebondit sur une table, puis repart dans l’autre sens. Le bruit conduit à une inscription qui dissipe les derniers doutes : « Fédération sénégalaise de tennis de table ». Une vingtaine de marches plus bas, la porte de droite ouvre sur un univers où la concentration est reine et les échanges s’enchaînent à un rythme soutenu. Adji Diéwo rêve du top 10 mondial Dans la salle, une dizaine de jeunes s’affrontent autour des tables bleues. Face à face, ils enchaînent les frappes et tentent de prendre leurs adversaires de vitesse. À chaque échange, la balle fuse d’un camp à l’autre. Une erreur, et il faut déjà se préparer au point suivant. Parmi eux, Adji Diewo s’emploie à retourner les balles d’un joueur plus âgé. La raquette bien en main, elle répond aux attaques, replace ses coups et se remet aussitôt en position. Lorsqu’une balle ne revient pas, une autre est déjà prête à prendre le relais. La jeune pongiste prend ensuite le temps d’expliquer les règles de cette discipline encore peu familière à de nombreux Sénégalais. « Les règles du tennis de table sont assez simples. La balle ne doit rebondir qu’une seule fois dans chaque partie de la table. Si elle rebondit deux fois du côté d’un joueur, celui-ci perd le point », explique-t-elle. Elle rappelle également que le joueur doit frapper la balle avec sa raquette sans la toucher plusieurs fois au cours d’un même renvoi. Adji Diewo fait partie des athlètes ayant effectué un stage en Chine pour préparer les JOJ. Une expérience intense, marquée par des journées d’entraînement bien remplies. « La préparation en Chine s’est très bien passée. Nous nous entraînions beaucoup : de 8 h à 11 h le matin, puis de 14 h à 18 h, tous les jours », raconte-t-elle. À ce séjour s’est ajouté un autre stage d’un mois au Sénégal. Si elle ne prendra pas part aux JOJ, la jeune athlète nourrit de grandes ambitions pour la suite de sa carrière. Elle veut porter haut les couleurs du Sénégal et du continent africain. « J’ambitionne de représenter le Sénégal et l’Afrique dans des compétitions internationales, de grimper au classement et de figurer dans le top 10 mondial », confie-t-elle. Un objectif qui exige, elle le sait, beaucoup de travail, de la discipline et une progression constante. Trois mois à fond sur les Joj Dans la salle, les entraînements se poursuivent sous le regard attentif de plusieurs encadreurs. Le président de la Fédération sénégalaise de tennis de table, Pape Anthioumane Diagne, participe lui-même aux séances. Dans un coin, les plus jeunes travaillent leurs réflexes autour d’une table. Ici, la moindre fraction de seconde peut faire la différence. La balle peut atteindre des vitesses élevées, ce qui impose aux joueurs une excellente coordination et une grande rapidité d’exécution. Sur une table longue de 2,74 mètres, les échanges ne laissent que peu de temps pour réfléchir. Pour Pape Anthioumane Diagne, la préparation des JOJ se déroule dans de bonnes conditions. Les pongistes sénégalais viennent notamment de participer au tournoi international WTT Youth Contender, au Caire, avant de prolonger leur séjour en Égypte par un camp d’entraînement. « L’équipe doit arriver ce dimanche au Sénégal. Elle disputait le tournoi international WTT Youth Contender au Caire. Les joueurs sont ensuite restés en Égypte pour un camp d’entraînement qui a pris fin ce samedi », explique le président de la fédération. Cette préparation s’inscrit dans un programme engagé depuis plusieurs mois. « Depuis plus de trois mois, nous sommes entièrement concentrés sur les JOJ. Avant ce tournoi, six joueurs s’étaient rendus en Chine pour un stage de 45 jours. Au fil des différentes étapes de sélection, le groupe s’est réduit. Au final, un garçon et une fille participeront aux Jeux », précise-t-il. Les deux représentants sénégalais seront engagés dans les épreuves individuelles masculine et féminine, ainsi qu’en double mixte. La fédération doit toutefois composer avec des moyens limités. « Nos ressources sont très limitées, mais le ministère des Sports et le Comité national olympique nous ont beaucoup facilité le travail en vue des JOJ », souligne Pape Anthioumane Diagne. « Les joueurs sont au top niveau » Du côté de l’encadrement technique, l’optimisme est également de mise. Pape Diack, qui dirigera l’équipe durant les Jeux, se réjouit du travail accompli au fil des stages et des regroupements. « La préparation se passe très bien, surtout après tous les stages auxquels nos jeunes ont pris part », estime le technicien. À leur retour au Sénégal, les athlètes bénéficieront de deux jours de repos avant d’entamer un nouveau regroupement interne de dix jours. Cette dernière phase doit permettre de peaufiner les automatismes et de préparer les joueurs aux exigences de la compétition. « Les joueurs sont au top niveau », assure Pape Diack. Le dernier rassemblement servira notamment à effectuer les ultimes réglages et à renforcer la préparation mentale. L’ambition est de réaliser une belle performance, sans perdre de vue l’essentiel : permettre aux jeunes pongistes de se mesurer à l’élite internationale et de tirer le meilleur parti de cette expérience. À Dakar, les JOJ seront aussi l’occasion de mettre en lumière des disciplines qui peinent encore à attirer l’attention du grand public. Avec ses échanges rapides, ses gestes précis et ses exigences techniques, le tennis de table entend profiter de cette exposition pour gagner en visibilité au Sénégal. Derrière les rebonds d’une petite balle blanche se dessinent ainsi de grandes ambitions : faire connaître la discipline, susciter de nouvelles vocations et préparer la relève du tennis de table sénégalais. Boubacar DIOP

items.title: PTI seeks production orders for 'detained' MNAs ahead of NA, Senate sessions
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The PTI requested the National Assembly speaker to issue production orders for its nine “detained” MNAs ahead of NA and Senate sessions on Tuesday. In a letter to NA Speaker Ayaz Sadiq, Chief Whip Amir Dogar claimed that the nine MNAs were “currently detained” and requested him to issue production orders for them to enable them to attend the 30th session starting today. The lawmakers comprised Haji Imtiaz Ahmad Choudhry (ΝΑ-68), Muhammad Jamal Ahsan Khan (NA-89), Mian Ghous Muhammad (ΝΑ-170), Sanaullah Khan Mastikhel (NΑ-91), Dawar Khan Kundi (NA-43), Junaid Akbar (NA-09), Amjad Ali Khan (NA-02), Fazal Muhammad Khan (ΝΑ-25) and Adil Khan Bazai (NA-262). “As the speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan, the impartiality of your esteemed office requires that production orders be issued for all detained members, irrespective of their political affiliation, to ensure that no constituency remains unrepresented during the proceedings of the House,” the letter read. It requested Sadiq to issue the production orders under Rule 108 of the 2007 Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the National Assembly. When the NA session began at around 7pm, Speaker Sadiq administered the oath of membership to PML-N’s Malik Munir Iqbal Channar, who won the Bahawalpur polls last month held to fill the seat of his late father Malik Muhammad Iqbal Channar. Lawmakers then offered prayers for late MNA Chaudhry Mahmood Bashir Virk, who died last month after a prolonged illness. As MNAs from various parties took their turns to recall the services of Virk, there was slight commotion, which prompted the speaker to urge PTI Chairman Gohar Ali Khan to respect the late MNA. Gohar remarked that sessions are usually adjourned after prayers for a deceased member. Referring to the governor’s rule in KP, he said the “funeral of this house was also held on Oct 11”. “We tried to give you very much in dialogue, but you (PTI) were not ready to take what we had offered,” the speaker replied, then switched off Gohar’s mic. The speaker said political discussion will not be allowed today, but tomorrow (Wednesday). PPP’s Syed Naveed Qamar also urged the PTI chairman to acknowledge the services of Virk, who had stood by the Constitution. He said the PTI could raise its issues later as well. Lawmakers then continued to pay tribute to Virk, with Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal among those who highlighted his professional life. President Asif Ali Zardari had summoned the sessions after he and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif agreed on it during their weekend meeting on the country’s political and security situation. The sessions also follow the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and emergency in 12 of its districts, for which the Centre cited the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. Earlier in the day, the NA Secretariat had shared the orders of the day for today’s session. Parliament approval for governor’s rule President Zardari had on Sunday issued proclamations of emergency and governor’s rule under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, respectively. According to Article 232, in case the president “acts on his own” — which was not the case for KP as he acted on PM Shehbaz’s advice — the proclamation of emergency is to be placed before both houses of Parliament for approval by each house within 10 days. It also empowers Parliament “to make laws for a province, or any part thereof, with respect to any matter not enumerated in the Federal Legislative List” during emergency. Meanwhile, a proclamation for governor’s rule issued under Article 234 “shall be laid before a joint sitting and shall cease to be in force at the expiration of two months, unless before the expiration of that period it has been approved by resolution of the joint sitting and may by like resolution be extended for a further period not exceeding two months at a time”. In the upper house, Senator Kamran Murtaza of the Jamiat Ulemai-i-Islam–Fazl (JUI-F) had submitted a resolution on Monday opposing the imposition of governor’s rule in KP. PM takes parties into confidence Ahead of the NA session, PM Shehbaz met with a parliamentary delegation comprising representatives of PML-Q, Balochistan Awami Party (BAP), Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party (IPP) and PML-Zia. The prime minister took the delegation into confidence regarding the situation in KP and explained the reasons behind the federal government’s decision to take constitutional measures, state-run APP reported. He said the conduct of the PTI-led KP government in the province and its failure to adopt an unequivocal stance against terrorism had posed risks to Pakistan’s growing economy. The premier highlighted that the federal government had provided more than Rs800 billion to KP under the National Finance Commission (NFC) arrangements to support efforts against terrorism. However, he said, the provincial government had failed to take effective measures to strengthen the capacity of its Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) and establish Safe City projects to improve its counterterrorism capabilities. According to the PM Office, the parliamentary delegation expressed its support for the federal government amid the prevailing situation and appreciated the prime minister’s leadership during what it described as difficult circumstances. The delegation also said the people of KP had remained deprived of adequate development in health, education and infrastructure during the PTI’s tenure in the province. It expressed confidence that, with the federal government’s cooperation, development and prosperity in KP would advance in line with other parts of the country. The delegation included BAP President and Science and Technology Minister Khalid Magsi; former Senate chairman Sadiq Sanjrani of BAP, senators Manzoor Kakar, Abdul Qadir Baloch, Dinesh Kumar and Samina Mumtaz Zehri; PML-Q President and Human Resource Development Minister Chaudhry Salik Hussain; and representatives of the IPP and PML-Zia. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Asif, Tarar, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry and PM’s Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah also attended the meeting. More to follow

items.title: Why Amaechi can’t win S’South for ADC – Wike
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has accused the vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress ADC, Rotimi Amaechi, of boasting that he removed two sons of the South-South, former President Goodluck Jonathan and former Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Walter Onnoghen, from their positions, and said that is why he cannot win the zone. Speaking at his monthly media chat in Abuja on Tuesday, Wike said Amaechi, a former governor of Rivers State, also did nothing for the zone as minister of transportation. Wike said Amaechi had claimed that history would remember him as the director general of a party’s campaign council that removed a sitting president. “Who was that sitting president? Jonathan. From where? South-South. A man from South-South boasted he removed a sitting president who is from South-South. You think the South-South people have forgotten that?” he asked. Wike said Amaechi also boasted that he “masterminded the removal” of Onnoghen, who he said also comes from the South-South. The minister then turned to Amaechi’s record in the Federal Executive Council. He pointed to the ports in Rivers, Calabar and Warri and said nothing had been done in the zone. “Now, the same man could not mastermind anything to help the South-South by making the ports to work. What has he now attracted to the South-South, to Rivers State, to make them then let us support him?” Wike asked. He also questioned the standing of the ADC, which he said was being treated as a major party before it had been tested at the polls. “How is it a major party? Have they won one councillorship?” he asked. Wike said he knew the party’s strategy and that it would fail in the region. “Nobody can cause crisis in the South-South. We know their strategy. And I can tell them it will not work,” he said. He said Amaechi had left out part of his own record when he spoke of how history would judge him. “But he didn’t tell Nigerians that history will also remember him as a DG who removed a sitting president, but who couldn’t get support from his state. He did not say that one,” Wike said. The post Why Amaechi can’t win S’South for ADC – Wike appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Don’t appoint your cheerleader as referee
items.description: President Mahama’s appointment of Emelia Afi Agbenyo as a Deputy Chairperson of the Electoral Commission raises a question that no impressive CV can answer: why burden an institution requiring public confidence with an avoidable controversy over political allegiance? The appointment is confirmed; reports identify her previous NDC campaign role and circulating posts supporting Mahama. Her competence is not the central issue. Neither is there any need to accuse her of intending to manipulate elections. She may possess exceptional ability and impeccable personal integrity. The concern is whether appointing someone publicly associated with one competitor demonstrates sound judgement when the office requires credible impartiality towards every competitor. Even an angel should not arrive at the referee’s table wearing yesterday’s campaign jersey. Good governance requires attention to actual, potential and perceived conflicts of interest. An electoral commissioner must exercise independent judgement. Citizens must also have reasonable grounds to trust that judgement. Appointments that create foreseeable doubts impose an unnecessary credibility burden on both the appointee and the institution. Constitutional authority answers who may appoint; wisdom addresses whom they should appoint. Mahama has instructed the new deputies to treat everyone fairly and give his government no preferential treatment. That assurance is welcome. But presidential instructions cannot erase a publicly established political association or substitute for careful selection. Trust should be protected at appointment, rather than repaired through speeches afterwards. The consequences extend beyond partisan argument. Where confidence deteriorates, routine administrative decisions become suspected schemes. Genuine mistakes become alleged conspiracies. An accurate electoral verdict may encounter rejection because citizens distrust the people delivering it. That creates a foreseeable national security risk: heightened tensions, inflammatory mobilisation and potentially violent confrontation. Such outcomes are neither inevitable nor justified. Political leaders nevertheless have a duty to avoid supplying unnecessary fuel. This standard must apply equally to the NDC, the NPP and every future government. Yesterday’s questionable appointment cannot legitimise today’s. Institutional damage does not become acceptable because opposing parties take turns inflicting it. The President should reconsider this appointment and explain the safeguards used to assess political impartiality. Ghana has capable citizens whose selection would inspire broader confidence. The nation deserves an electoral referee whose appointment does not begin with an argument about which team she supports.

items.title: Última hora de la visita de los Reyes a Ceuta, en directo | Vivas avisa de que Ceuta “es una olla a presión que en cualquier momento puede estallar”
items.description: El rey Felipe VI y la reina Letizia han comenzado este martes una visita a Ceuta, casi dos meses y medio después de la entrada masiva de unos 70.000 inmigrantes desde la frontera marroquí entre el 30 y el 31 de julio. Los Reyes, que buscan trasladar el apoyo de la monarquía a la sociedad ceutí, han llegado a las 12.30 a la Gran Vía, donde los esperaba una marea de ceutíes. Después se han desplazado hasta el Ayuntamiento de la ciudad autónoma para mantener un encuentro con el presidente Juan Jesús Vivas y el mando único en la ciudad autónoma, el ministro Ángel Víctor Torres. Tras el encuentro, el presidente ceutí ha advertido de que la ciudad atraviesa el momento “más difícil de su historia reciente” y se ha convertido “en una olla a presión que en cualquier momento puede estallar”. Esta tarde, los Reyes tendrán varios actos sociales y pernoctarán en la ciudad autónoma para desplazarse a Melilla el miércoles. Ambas ciudades llevan 19 años sin recibir la visita de un jefe del Estado, desde que Juan Carlos I y doña Sofía viajaron en 2007. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Army conducts successful test launch of hypersonic Fatah-2 extended range missile: ISPR
items.description: The Pakistan Army successfully test-launched the Fatah-2 extended range (ER) hypersonic ballistic missile, the military’s media wing said in a statement on Tuesday. According to Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the Fatah-2 ER is equipped with advanced navigation and state-of-the-art avionics. “It is capable of engaging targets with high precision and defeating [the] enemy’s missile defence systems due to its unique trajectory and manoeuvrability features,” it added. “Fatah-2 ER, with its extended range, will further enhance [the] army’s reach and capability of engaging deep targets.” The test launch was witnessed by Army Rocket Force Command (ARFC) chief Lt Gen Nauman Zakaria, senior army officers, scientists and engineers. The ARFC commander “appreciated the dedication and technical prowess of scientists and engineers”, ISPR said. It further said the president, prime minister, and the chief of defence forces congratulated the scientists and engineers on the successful test launch of the “extended range version of Fatah-2 weapon system”. Last week, the indigenously developed extended version of the Fatah-IV ground-launched cruise missile also underwent a successful test launch . In a statement, ISPR said, “Equipped with advanced avionics and state-of-the-art navigational aids, the weapon system is capable of engaging targets at extended ranges with high precision and lethality.” “The test also validated additional technical parameters of various sub-systems incorporated for improved accuracy and enhanced survivability,” it added. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi congratulated the nation on the success of the test. In a statement on X, he said: “The scientists and engineers of the Pakistan Army have accomplished a matter of pride.” He added that it was an important advancement in the defence sector.

items.title: Ilias Akhomach s’exprime sur la polémique du T-shirt de Sebta
items.description: Ilias Akhomach a réagi à la polémique autour du T-shirt de Sebta, qui a suscité des réactions impliquant notamment Ez Abde, Kylian Mbappé et Vinicius Junior. Le joueur estime que chacun est libre de ses choix et appelle à ne pas mêler football et politique. La polémique autour du T-shirt de Sebta continue de faire réagir dans le monde du football. Cette fois, c’est Ilias Akhomach qui a pris la parole pour donner son point de vue sur cette affaire, marquée par les interrogations autour de la décision de certains joueurs de porter ou non ce maillot. Pour l’international marocain, cette controverse a pris une ampleur disproportionnée. Il estime qu’il s’agit d’une polémique « créée de toutes pièces » par le public et les journalistes, alors que les joueurs devraient avant tout se concentrer sur leur activité sportive. « Chacun est libre de faire ce qu’il veut. Je trouve normal que certains portent ce maillot et que d’autres non. Chacun est libre de ses choix, et je ne pense pas que ce soit un sujet de conversation » , a-t-il déclaré. Dans ses déclarations, Ilias Akhomach insiste sur la nécessité de distinguer le terrain des débats politiques. Selon lui, les joueurs sont avant tout présents pour disputer des rencontres de football et offrir un spectacle au public, sans être contraints de prendre position sur des questions qui dépassent le cadre sportif. « Nous allons jouer un match de football, nous ne voulons pas nous mêler de politique ni de débats », a-t-il affirmé. Le joueur reconnaît néanmoins que les footballeurs sont conscients des difficultés et des problèmes qui existent dans le monde. Il estime toutefois que leur rôle ne leur permet pas nécessairement d’agir sur ces questions, soulignant que les décisions relèvent avant tout des responsables politiques. « Bien sûr, nous soutenons Sebta et nous sommes conscients des nombreux problèmes du monde, mais nous ne sommes personne pour changer les choses. C’est le rôle des politiciens de le faire », a-t-il expliqué, tout en précisant ne pas vouloir s’impliquer dans des questions dont il ne maîtrise pas tous les mécanismes. Le football avant les controverses À travers cette prise de parole, Ilias Akhomach défend une approche centrée sur le sport et sur la liberté individuelle des joueurs. Pour lui, le fait de porter ou de refuser un maillot relève d'un choix personnel qui ne devrait pas systématiquement donner lieu à des controverses. L’international marocain rappelle également la vocation première du football : permettre aux supporters de vivre un bon moment et de profiter du spectacle. « Tout ce que je sais, c’est que nous allons jouer un match de football, pour que les gens passent un bon moment et s’amusent », a-t-il conclu. Cette déclaration intervient dans un contexte où les prises de position, les gestes symboliques et les choix vestimentaires des footballeurs peuvent rapidement susciter des débats qui dépassent le cadre des compétitions. La polémique autour du T-shirt de Sebta illustre ainsi la difficulté, pour certains joueurs, de préserver une séparation entre leur carrière sportive et les enjeux politiques ou symboliques associés à leur image publique. The post Ilias Akhomach s’exprime sur la polémique du T-shirt de Sebta appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Ghana needs stronger international cooperation to fight cybercrime – CSA
items.description: Ghana needs stronger international cooperation to tackle cybercrime as digital threats increasingly cross national borders, Director-General of the Cyber Security Authority (CSA), Dr Divine Selase Agbeti, has said. He said Ghana could not address the growing cybersecurity threat alone, particularly as businesses, financial systems and public services became increasingly interconnected. Speaking at the 2026 Morocco Cybersecurity Week in Rabat, Dr Agbeti called on African countries to strengthen cooperation between their cybersecurity agencies and foreign affairs ministries to improve responses to cyber threats. He said collaboration should include sharing threat intelligence, conducting joint exercises and coordinating responses to cyber incidents affecting multiple countries. “Cyber diplomacy has become an important instrument for advancing national interests, building trust and facilitating cooperation on issues affecting cyberspace,” he said. Dr Agbeti said stronger international cooperation could help Ghanaian businesses and authorities respond more effectively to cybercrime originating abroad or involving criminal networks operating across multiple jurisdictions. He cautioned, however, that international partnerships must deliver practical benefits rather than remain limited to agreements and declarations. “International partnerships should respond to national priorities, support sustainable capacity development and equip our institutions to manage cybersecurity risks independently over time,” he said. The CSA Director-General also called for stronger national cybersecurity institutions, better coordination among government agencies and increased investment in technical skills. He urged African countries to deepen collaboration with regional organisations, development partners, universities and the private sector to strengthen their ability to prevent and respond to cyber incidents. Dr Agbeti said the success of international cybersecurity cooperation should be measured by whether it improved incident response, information-sharing and the resilience of Africa’s digital systems. He stressed that the continent’s digital future would depend not only on how quickly countries adopted new technologies, but also on how effectively they secured those technologies and built public trust in them.

items.title: La Fondation Orange Guinée & ses partenaires – en collaboration avec le Ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène Publique ; le Ministère de la Femme, Famille et Solidarité – lancent le Programme Santé 3.0
items.description: Communiqué de presse Conakry, le 12 octobre 2026 Le 7 octobre 2026, aux côtés de ses partenaires et en présence des Secrétaires Généraux des deux départements ministériels , Dr Mory KEITA du MSHP et Mr Saa Kossa TOURE du MFFS, a été lancé le Programme Santé 3.0 , une initiative qui regroupe 11 acteurs mobilisés autour d’un seul objectif : agir en faveur de la santé et du bien-être des populations guinéennes. Le Programme Santé 3.0, fruit d’un partenariat public privé ambitieux, est un programme de santé pluridisciplinaire qui se traduit par une approche structurée, séquencée et durable. Il apporte des solutions concrètes aux défis enregistrés en matière d’accès aux soins de santé au sein des communautés, plus précisément sur des maladies évitables dont les statistiques disponibles indiquent une progression rapide en plus du rajeunissement et des taux de prévalence élevés chez les femmes. Les maladies ciblées par ce consortium sont : le diabète, l’hypertension artérielle, les maladies auditives, le cancer du col de l’utérus, le paludisme, la santé sexuelle et reproductive. L’initiative de la Fondation Orange Guinée porte l’ambition partagée des partenaires ci-après, tous engagés sur une mise en œuvre durant 3 ans : Le Ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène Publique à travers entre autres la Direction Nationale de la Promotion de la santé, la Direction de la santé Communautaire, la Direction Nationale de la Lutte contre la Maladie Le Ministère de la Femme, Famille et Solidarité à travers la Direction Nationale des Personnes Vulnérables et celle du Fonds de Développement Social et de l’Indigence Le Programme national de lutte contre les maladies non transmissibles (PNLMNT), Le Programme national de lutte contre le paludisme (PNLP) , Le Programme national de Lutte contre le Cancer (PNLC) La Société Civile (CNOSCG) L’ Organisation mondiale de la Santé (OMS) , Le Fonds des Nations unies pour la population (UNFPA) , La Croix-Rouge Guinéenne (CRG) , Sante en Entreprise Santé Intégrée Solthis , Visa Médical et Sanofi Tous unissent leurs expertises pour renforcer la prévention, le dépistage, la prise en charge et l’accès aux soins, notamment dans les zones décentralisées, au plus près des communautés. Le Programme Santé 3.0 se déploiera autour de trois leviers complémentaires : La formation des agents de santé communautaires , afin de renforcer leurs capacités d’écoute, de prévention, d’orientation et d’accompagnement des patients ; Le déploiement d’une caravane mobile , proposant consultations, dépistage, conseils et orientation médicale dans les localités ciblées ; La sensibilisation et prévention en continue, pour encourager la prévention, le dépistage précoce et le recours aux services de santé disponibles à proximité. Ce lancement ouvre surtout une séquence de déploiement progressif avec le démarrage des formations dans les localités retenues précédent la 1ere caravane mobile M Ousmane Boly TRAORE, Président de la Fondation Orange Guinée confirmera d’ailleurs « Avec le Programme Santé 3.0, nous franchissons une nouvelle étape de notre engagement en faveur du bien-être des Guinéens. Notre ambition est d’agir collectivement et dans la durée pour renforcer la prévention, le dépistage et l’accès aux soins, au plus près des populations. » Le Programme Santé 3.0 place l’humain au cœur de son action pour encore mieux accompagner les communautés, soutenir les agents de santé et les relais communautaires, et assurer un impact concret des actions menées sur le terrain. À travers cette initiative,1ere en son genre en Guinée, à la fois le MSHP, le MFFS, la Fondation Orange Guinée et l’ensemble des partenaires engagés affirment leur volonté de faire de la santé de proximité une réalité forte d’une véritable coordination garante d’une pérennité au service des guinéens et guinéennes. À propos de la Fondation Orange Guinée La Fondation Orange Guinée s’engage pour un accès égal à l’éducation, la santé et la culture. Ses programmes entendent contribuer à l’amélioration de la santé maternelle et infantile et la santé du 3 e âge ; au renforcement de l’employabilité des jeunes, l’autonomisation des femmes ; la réinsertion et employabilité des jeunes et la préservation du patrimoine culturel. Avec plus d’un million de personnes touchées par ses programmes, elle a pour ambition en 2024 de continuer à agir pour contribuer à la construction d’une société plus inclusive, une société dans laquelle le numérique est un des leviers incontournables du développement humain de chaque guinéen. En savoir plus : https://www.orange-guinee.com/fr/fondation.html

items.title: Declare your stance on petrol pricing – Agbakoba tells presidential candidates
items.description: A former president of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) Dr Olisa Agbakoba has demanded that 2027 presidential candidates should publicly state their stance on petroleum pricing. Agbakoba made this known in a statement he personally signed on Tuesday in Lagos. The former NBA president described fuel costs as a likely deciding issue for voters. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the statement is titled: “Statement to the Presidential Candidates on Petroleum Pricing and the Cost of Living. Agbakoba stated that the skyrocketing cost of living in Nigeria has reached a critical point and would undoubtedly serve as a defining issue in the 2027 general election. He said: “Nigeria removed its petrol subsidy in 2023, and pump prices now move with refinery and import landing costs rather than being fixed by the government. “The effect has been steep. In January, NNPC Ltd., sold petrol at ₦835 per litre in Lagos and ₦839 in Abuja. “NNPC retail’s regular price in Abuja is now ₦1,405, while stations backed by the Dangote refinery and independent marketers are selling at ₦1,405 to ₦1,409. “Dangote Petroleum Refinery raised its gantry price to ₦1,350 per litre on 12 September, its fourth increase since late August, before a ₦25 cut later that month.” Agbakoba pointed out that high pump prices were feeding through the economy. “High fuel prices have created a severe domino effect, driving up the costs of transport, food, rent, education, and basic consumer goods across the board. “Nigerian voters urgently need clarity on where each presidential candidate stands on this vital matter,” he said. He identified four possible fuel policy scenarios. Agbakoba said these included total subsidy removal, a return to subsidies, a discount pricing approach and differential pricing, urging the candidates to make their stance known. (NAN) The post Declare your stance on petrol pricing – Agbakoba tells presidential candidates appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: CSA warns of growing cyber threats as Ghana’s digital dependence increases
items.description: The Cyber Security Authority (CSA) has warned that Ghana’s growing dependence on digital services is exposing consumers, businesses and critical infrastructure to increasingly complex cyber threats. The Authority’s Director-General, Dr Divine Selase Agbeti, said cybercrime, online fraud, ransomware and attacks on critical infrastructure were becoming greater concerns as African economies relied more heavily on digital platforms. Speaking at the 2026 Morocco Cybersecurity Week in Rabat, he said the growing interconnection between financial systems, businesses and public services meant that cyberattacks could have consequences beyond the countries in which they originated. “Cybersecurity is no longer simply a technical matter,” he said, describing it as an issue of national security, economic stability, governance and public trust. Cyber risks extend beyond institutions Dr Agbeti said the risks associated with digital dependence were no longer confined to large organisations. In Ghana, digital platforms are increasingly used for payments, commerce, communication, education and other essential services. Disruptions to these systems could affect how consumers access services and carry out everyday transactions. He said differences in national laws, regulatory frameworks and response capabilities made it more difficult for countries to tackle cyber incidents that crossed borders. “A cyber incident originating in one country can disrupt essential services in another,” he said. Dr Agbeti therefore called for stronger cooperation among African countries, including information-sharing and coordinated responses to cyber incidents. Laws must be backed by resources The CSA Director-General said Ghana had established a legal framework for cybersecurity through the Cybersecurity Act, 2020 (Act 1038), which provides for the identification and protection of critical information infrastructure. However, he cautioned that legislation alone would not be sufficient to address evolving threats. He said countries needed adequately resourced cybersecurity institutions and skilled personnel capable of responding to emerging risks. Dr Agbeti said stronger cybersecurity measures would be essential for Ghana and other African countries to benefit from digital transformation while protecting consumers, businesses and essential services from cyber threats.

items.title: 'Holding our ground': Israel demolishes dozens of Bedouin homes
items.description: Under an overcast sky in southern Israel, Bedouin villagers wandered through the rubble of what used to be their homes, the latest to be demolished after being deemed illegal structures by Israeli authorities. The residents of Al-Dahiya in the Negev desert say they have nowhere else to go after bulldozers destroyed around 80 structures housing some 400 people on Monday. "When night falls, where are we supposed to sleep? Under the open sky, or by the light of the moon -- if there is a moon," said 65-year-old Muhammad Abu Wadi.

items.title: Futsal : la CAF salue la démonstration du Maroc face à l’Algérie
items.description: Vainqueur de l’Algérie (4-0) pour son entrée en lice à la CAN de futsal 2026, le Maroc a marqué les esprits. La Confédération africaine de football (CAF) a salué la performance des Lions de l’Atlas, qui ont idéalement lancé leur campagne de défense du titre continental. Le Maroc a réussi ses débuts à domicile. Dans un article publié mardi 13 octobre, la CAF est revenue sur la victoire des Lions de l’Atlas face à l’Algérie, lundi soir à Rabat, lors de la première journée du groupe A de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations de futsal 2026. L’instance continentale a mis en avant l’efficacité des hommes de Hicham Dguig, qui ont rapidement pris le contrôle de la rencontre. Younes Makkarssi a ouvert le score à la 10e minute, avant que Youssef Jouad ne creuse l’écart deux minutes plus tard, permettant au Maroc d’aborder la suite du match avec davantage de sérénité. Jouad a ensuite confirmé sa grande performance en inscrivant deux nouveaux buts aux 26e et 32e minutes. Auteur d’un triplé, il a été désigné meilleur joueur de la rencontre, récompensant sa contribution majeure au succès marocain. Les Lions de l’Atlas lancent leur campagne La CAF a également souligné les difficultés de la sélection algérienne, qui participe pour la première fois de son histoire à la phase finale de la compétition. Malgré une approche défensive destinée à limiter les offensives marocaines, les Algériens n’ont pas réussi à trouver le chemin des filets. Grâce à cette victoire sans appel, le Maroc envoie un premier message à ses concurrents et affiche ses ambitions dans cette édition organisée sur son sol. Les Lions de l’Atlas devront désormais confirmer cette dynamique lors des prochaines rencontres. La sélection marocaine affrontera la Zambie mercredi 14 octobre, avant de retrouver la Libye vendredi 16 octobre pour son dernier match de groupe. Deux rendez-vous importants pour poursuivre sur cette lancée et se rapprocher d’un nouveau sacre continental. The post Futsal : la CAF salue la démonstration du Maroc face à l’Algérie appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Liverpool trio Isak, Gakpo, Szoboszlai to miss LASK clash
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Liverpool will be without Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai for Wednesday’s UEFA Champions League clash against LASK following injuries sustained during the international break. According to ESPN, the three players have failed to recover in time for the encounter at Austria’s Raiffeisen Arena and were excluded from Liverpool’s 23-man travelling squad. The trio also missed Liverpool’s 3-0 defeat to Manchester City on Sunday after suffering different injury setbacks while on international duty. Isak withdrew from international duty with a thigh injury, while Gakpo sustained an ankle injury. Szoboszlai returned from Hungary’s camp with a tight hamstring. Speaking about Szoboszlai’s fitness at the weekend, Liverpool manager Iraola said: “Dom came from the national team with tightness, an overload. We put him as a floater in the training and tried to protect him but he was feeling something very small. It’s true that now we play four games in 10 days, so it’s going to be difficult because we fly to Austria in two days. I think it’s going to be difficult to recover any of the players.” Liverpool are now expected to provide further updates on the players’ fitness ahead of Wednesday’s match, with the club’s manager scheduled to address the media at a pre-match news conference on Tuesday.
