items.title: PAC pushes for effective use of GH¢25m by Tree Crops Development Authority
items.description: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) has urged the Tree Crops Development Authority to make productive use of about GH¢25 million in its account to support its operations and growth. The Authority regulates the cashew, coconut, oil palm, rubber, mango and shea sectors and has provided training for farmers to improve their yields. The Committee made the call on the fifth day of public hearings on the 2025 audit reports, during which it commended the Authority’s Chief Executive Officer, Dr Andy Osei Okrah, and his management team for their work. The Committee, however, urged the management to sustain its efforts and obtain vehicle ownership documents for vehicles purchased for the institution. In a related development, the Committee directed Dr Benedict Bonaventure Aligeba, former Managing Director of the Irrigation Company of Upper Region Limited (ICOUR), to vacate the official bungalow after the one-year retirement period. The Cocoa Processing Company Limited was also cited for procurement breaches in the 2025 Auditor-General’s Report. The Committee advised the company to comply with the Public Procurement Act, 2003 (Act 663), as amended, which regulates the procurement of goods, works and services using public funds. It also advised the company to enrol on the Ghana Electronic Procurement System (GHANEPS).

items.title: Why the Intelligence Gap Really Matters
items.description: E arlier this year , a woman posted on Threads that a man she had been dating dumped her after discovering that she had a library card. She shared a screenshot of what she said was the man’s “breakup text,” in which the writer accused her of “wasting hours” like “some little kid playing pretend smart” and excoriated her for failing to satisfy him sexually: “Reading books? Really? While I’m sitting here with actual needs!!” The internet, of course, reacted. Memes and think pieces abounded. These responses weren’t just gasps of outrage at the man’s dismissal of literacy and his base sense of entitlement. They also captured a particular kind of anxiety about a sometimes highly sensitive question related to romantic compatibility: What happens when you and your partner are on a different intellectual plane? I didn’t always have language for this type of gap. Growing up and attending church, I heard a lot about the biblical caution to “not be unequally yoked” to a mate, invoked to warn Christians against consorting with nonbelievers. As I developed my own intellectual practice, during which I grew to believe that many sacred texts were best read figuratively, I came to understand the biblical advice differently. To be equally yoked meant to walk forward together without one pulling harder than the other. Basically, you don’t want one member of the pair to be missing the beat. Over the years I worked on my doctoral dissertation, about the brilliant and tortured John Milton, my adviser and mentor was the acclaimed Miltonist Francis C. Blessington . In many of our conversations, he spoke fondly about the wit and wisdom of his wife, Ann Taylor, also a professor, and a writer in a completely different field. As a young person, I think I took for granted the kind of similitude this couple shared. At Blessington’s memorial service last fall, I eulogized him and met Taylor in person for the first time. She spoke about their intellectual companionship with such love and specificity that it stopped me. They didn’t work in matching fields, and they didn’t have identical minds. But they were two people whose depths met. In reflecting on my mentor and his wife, I couldn’t help thinking that Mr. Breakup Text, in revealing what lay within his depths, at least did the woman he’d been dating a favor. Better for her to know about his disposition sooner rather than later. I also had no doubt that John Milton himself—who in 1643 nearly destroyed his reputation arguing that intellectual incompatibility should be legal grounds for divorce—would have agreed with me. I n the summer of 1642, Milton married Mary Powell. In short order, she left him. Milton’s response was to do what many intellectuals do when their personal life implodes: He turned his crisis into theory. In 1643, he published The Doctrine & Discipline of Divorce , which made a bold claim that marriage should be dissolvable when spouses are cerebrally incompatible. The backlash was immediate and severe. Divorce in 17th-century England was nearly impossible, granted only for the most extreme circumstances (abuse, for instance, or infidelity). But Milton wasn’t arguing about tangible, provable transgressions. He was arguing about loneliness—the specific, suffocating loneliness of living with someone whose mind you cannot reach. For doing so, he was effectively canceled. His argument was anchored by a close reading of Genesis. When God created Eve as a “help meet” for Adam, Milton suggested, she was not meant to be simply a body for procreation or a servant for labor. If that were all Adam needed, God could have given him anyone. What Adam required was a person he could speak with—a source of “apt and cheerfull conversation,” someone with whom to share thoughts, to reason, to find the companionship of mind that makes solitude bearable. And when that communion is absent? Milton had a word for it: bondage. He wrote that to couple two souls whose minds don’t meet is to join “a living soule” to “a dead corps.” Marriage devoid of intellectual intimacy isn’t merely disappointing. It is a form of living death, worse than being alone, because at least in solitude you aren’t confronted daily with the failure of connection. [ Read: The tyranny of the relationship gap ] Milton’s most radical claim was that intellectual incompatibility is a more serious problem than adultery. “He who affirms adultery to be the highest breach,” he wrote, “affirms the bed to be the highest of mariage, which is in truth a grosse and borish opinion.” Adultery within a marriage can be overcome, he believed. A mismatch of intelligences cannot. He then went further, mocking the Church of England for being more concerned with resolving a lack of conjugal relations—“the disappointing of an impetuous nerve”—than with “the ingenuous grievance of a minde unreasonably yoakt.” To him, intellectual companionship outranked sex not just as a nice feature of marriage but as its entire foundation. That was a radical notion in 1643 (and, I would argue, it remains so). Milton’s insistence that wives be intellectual companions to their husbands was progressive for the 17th century because it implied that women were capable of rational thought and meaningful conversation. His view ran counter to prevailing beliefs, which said that, at most, a wife should be educated enough to converse with her husband but not so educated that she might challenge his authority. Across the centuries, other writers and philosophers have considered the importance of intellectual parity between the sexes. In the mid-1700s, a group of Englishwomen known as the bluestockings created salons where serious conversation was the point, and where women’s minds were not secondary to men’s. (That the term bluestocking became a slur demonstrates how threatened broader society remained at the idea of women as intellectuals.) Nearly 250 years after Milton, Nietzsche engaged with the question of cerebral compatibility from a slightly different direction. In his 1878 book, Human, All Too Human , he argued that marriage is fundamentally a long conversation, and that when choosing a partner, you should ask whether you can talk well with that person into old age. L ike Milton, Nietzsche characterized intellectual communion as fundamental to a lasting union, not as a bonus. I align with the thinking of both. But the person who really helped me answer the question of what matters in romance, the mind or the body—or whether those distinctions are even useful—was not someone I read. It was someone I listened to: the lyrical philosopher known as Prince. I’ve spent a good part of my career thinking about music as a form of knowledge. But Prince had me long before any of that. I was captivated by his creative fluency, the way he moved from intellect to physicality to spirituality without ever treating them as separate domains, let alone ranking them. If I were to sketch a longer trajectory of those rankings on the way to Prince, it might go something like this: Saint Augustine built a bridge between the sacred and the profane that Western thought has been living inside ever since. In the 14th century, the Italian scholar-poet Petrarch elevated love by spiritualizing it, positioning the beloved as an untouchable muse—adored from afar, beautiful precisely because she was unreachable. Milton imagined intellectual communion as divine but didn’t connect it to the body. In the 19th century, Percy Bysshe Shelley argued for a fusion of souls , describing the concept of the “twin flame”: “We shall become the same, we shall be one / Spirit within two frames, oh! wherefore two? / One passion in twin-hearts, which grows and grew.” Nietzsche abandoned the sacred entirely and kept only the mind. And much of 20th-century pop culture (especially in music) swung the other way, reducing attraction to the body alone. Prince knocked all the walls down. Where Petrarch’s lover might have written “I love you so much I could die,” Prince took the conceit and made it visceral, carnal, immediate—then turned around and insisted that the mind was what he was really after. Many people register Prince’s hypersexual image and miss the consistent thread of yearning for intellectual intimacy running through his music. In “ If I Was Your Girlfriend ,” he doesn’t position himself as a conqueror. He asks to be repositioned as a confidant, someone granted access to a woman’s unperformed interior world. The song isn’t seduction. It’s a plea for the kind of knowing that Milton called “meet help” and that Nietzsche called “a long conversation.” Prince just set his lines to a drum machine. [ From the September 2026 issue: The great romance slump ] Even in “ Sexy M.F. ,” in which the surface is pure provocation, Prince insists that what he wants is “not your body, your mind, you fool.” The argument for intellectual intimacy is embedded inside the most overtly physical song imaginable because Prince refused to separate the categories. On “ Love 2 the 9’s ,” you can hear him testing what some psychologists refer to as “cognitive tempo” in real time. The track is structured as rapid-fire banter with the artist’s creative collaborator and eventual wife Mayte Garcia, a back-and-forth in which wit, timing, and verbal dexterity are the point. It’s flirtation, but the flirtation is the assessment. Can she keep pace? Can she volley? Prince isn’t just charming her. He’s running Milton’s compatibility test on tape. The artist’s 1996 three-disc album, Emancipation , released simultaneously as a declaration of freedom from Warner Bros. and a celebration of his marriage to Garcia, fuses romantic partnership with creative autonomy. The track “ Friend, Lover, Sister, Mother/Wife ” collapses every form of intimacy—companionable, lustful, familial, marital—into one person. His vision wasn’t Milton’s hierarchy or Nietzsche’s abstraction; it was total fusion. He wasn’t asking whether his partner knew what he knew. He was asking: Can we know each other completely? T hough Prince’s vision was extraordinary, not even he could sustain it, in practice. His marriage to Garcia ended in divorce after the loss of their son; his second marriage also ended in divorce. Which brings us back to the question: What, in practice—and amid the chaos of modern life—is actually achievable? I have come to believe that what sustains intellectual intimacy is not a shared knowledge base or level of education but rather three elements operating together. When even one is missing, the whole thing may falter. The first element is curiosity. Here, I don’t mean that people must be curious about the same things. Rather, each needs to show a willingness to care about what the other person deeply cares about. What are you reading? is a question about someone’s day. What are you enjoying about it? is a question about the person. The second element is a shared language—the ability to pick up what the other person is putting down, without a decoder ring—meaning the shorthand that you use, the references that land, and the nuance that doesn’t need to be spelled out. In the field of rhetoric, this is described as a “discourse community,” a relationship between individuals that is solidified, in part, by their norms of communication. The third is mental timing: having the same cadence of wit, the same processing speed, the ability to volley and return. This is what Prince showed off in “Love 2 the 9’s.” It’s what researchers studying interpersonal synchrony are now measuring at a biological level, because when people truly click, they’re literally falling into rhythm, matching heart rates and brain waves. In musical performance, coherence doesn’t come from sameness but from attunement. Musicians listen for structure, timing, and possibility. They respond, adjust, and extend. They are, in a sense, thinking together. Relationships work the same way. What we experience as being “seen” is often a shared capacity to track and respond to each other’s signals. Two people can inhabit entirely different domains and still meet each other with immediacy, grasping nuance, appreciating enthusiasm, building on each other’s ideas rather than flattening them. The real intellectual gap in relationships, then, isn’t between knowing ball or knowing Aristotle, to paraphrase Taylor Swift—because the issue isn’t whether your partner knows what you know. More important is the difference between disinterest and curiosity, between aloofness and care, between “You’re boring me” and “I don’t get it yet, but tell me more.” Some people may think that worrying about intellectual compatibility is precious or elitist. But centuries of thinkers agree that minds matter, conversation matters, and being mentally alone with someone you share a life with is a particular kind of suffering worth taking seriously. My advice? Find a person who wants to hear about what you’re reading, not just someone who waits for you to close the book. ​​When you buy a book using a link on this page, we receive a commission. items.title: UK MEET Fellowship challenges journalists to look beyond AI hype
items.description: Journalists and digital content creators have been challenged to scrutinise claims about emerging technologies and demand evidence before presenting them to the public. The call was made on Monday, October 12, during the opening of the UK Media Excellence for Emerging Technologies (UK MEET) Fellowship in Accra. The five-day programme brings together selected media professionals to strengthen their capacity to report on science, technology and innovation, with a focus on distinguishing evidence-based findings from exaggerated claims. As artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies become increasingly prominent in healthcare, education and other sectors, the programme seeks to equip journalists with the skills to examine what these innovations can deliver, their limitations and their potential impact on society. Welcoming participants on behalf of the British High Commission, Ryan Davies highlighted the need for stronger and more sustainable connections between researchers and media practitioners. He stressed that as technological developments advance rapidly, trusted journalism is essential to helping the public navigate misinformation and understand the implications of scientific discoveries. Separating scientific evidence from marketing claims The opening day featured a fireside conversation on artificial intelligence in healthcare, with Darlington Akogo, founder of Mino Health AI Labs examining the difference between real-world clinical applications and marketing hype. The discussion placed the spotlight on the questions journalists should ask when reporting on technological innovations, including what evidence supports developers’ claims, how a tool performs in practice and whether its benefits can be independently verified. The issue is particularly important as AI systems are increasingly promoted for applications that could affect people’s health, education and access to essential services. For journalists, reporting on such developments requires more than explaining how a technology works. It also involves examining its reliability, limitations and consequences for the people expected to depend on it. Connecting research to public understanding The fellowship also highlighted the importance of making scientific knowledge accessible beyond academic and research institutions. Delivering the opening keynote, Director of the Ghana National Research Fund, Professor Abigail Opoku-Mensah, called for increased domestic investment in research and innovation, alongside closer collaboration between journalists and researchers. Abigail Opoku-Mensah, GNRF. She said stronger local financing would help Ghana build a sustainable research ecosystem and reduce long-term dependence on external support. Established under Act 1056 and officially launched in June 2025, the Fund is mandated to support research and innovation in priority areas, including health, food systems, climate sustainability, digital and industrial technologies, and governance. Prof. Opoku-Mensah urged journalists to help translate scientific developments into information citizens can understand and use, stressing that public communication is essential to turning research investments into meaningful outcomes. From training to investigative storytelling The UK MEET Fellowship is delivered by Imperial College London through Imperial Global Ghana, with support from the British High Commission. It seeks to strengthen science, technology and innovation reporting among journalists and digital content creators in Ghana and Nigeria. Participants will engage with researchers, policymakers and technology experts while developing original story pitches on emerging technologies. Ten participants with the strongest pitches will be selected for an educational visit to Imperial College London. The programme covers areas including artificial intelligence, climate and environmental risks, biomedical innovation and the circular economy. Its broader ambition is to strengthen evidence-based journalism and ensure that public conversations about technological progress are informed by credible information rather than unverified promises.

items.title: Kurt Okraku’s regime has ‘failed to perform’ – Kudjoe Fianoo demands resignation of GFA Executive Council
items.description: Former Ghana League Clubs Association (GHALCA) chairman Kudjoe Fianoo has called on Ghana Football Association (GFA) president Kurt Okraku and the entire Executive Council to resign, accusing the current administration of failing to deliver on expectations since taking office in October 2019. According to the former AshantiGold CEO, the present administration has “failed to perform” on expectations since taking office in October 2019. “You can give him an excuse in your first four years, or even in your first two years. But if it is not progressing, it is rather regressing,” Fianoo told Graphic Sports. “He headed a body that failed to perform. So they should all leave,” he added. Kurt has come under increasing pressure amid the Black Stars’ recent struggles, with Ghana suffering a disappointing start to their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign. The Black Stars lost 4-2 at home to The Gambia in their second Group C match, following a defeat by Ivory Coast in their opening qualifier. Those results have left Ghana without a point from their first two matches and bottom of Group C, while Ivory Coast and The Gambia lead the standings with six points each. The Black Stars, who are currently undergoing technical changes, are scheduled to return to action in November when they face Somalia at the Accra Sports Stadium.

Afenyo-Markin’s influence is limited by minority numbers in Parliament – Haruna Iddrisu
items.description: Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu says Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin is doing his best in Parliament but faces limited influence because of the numerical strength of his caucus. The former Minority Leader reflected on the challenges of leading an opposition caucus against a substantially larger majority. “For instance, the current minority leader, Afeyo Makin, is doing his utmost best, but he’s simply overwhelmed with the numbers,” he said while discussing on JoyFM’s SMS on Tuesday. “Very little to do, very little influence with those numbers,” he added. Mr Iddrisu compared the situation with his own experience in a Parliament where the distribution of seats significantly limited the opposition’s ability to influence proceedings. “So it reminded me of my days when we had 169, 106 kind of Parliament, where you can be told that even if you walk out, it made no meaning and made no consequence,” he said. Despite those numerical differences, the Tamale South MP stressed that democracy required space for dissent and constructive criticism. “But I think that for the good of our democracy, it’s good to tolerate dissent, and it’s good to tolerate constructive criticisms,” he said. He explained that such criticism should help improve governance and the quality of life of Ghanaians, adding that making life easier for citizens should be the primary objective of public office holders. Mr Iddrisu also underscored the importance of consensus in parliamentary leadership, noting that leaders sometimes needed to allow backbenchers to take the initiative before intervening to manage disagreements. “Consensus is the beauty of any democracy,” he said. His remarks came in response to questions about whether he missed parliamentary leadership and how he viewed the conduct of parliamentary business.

items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has commended the current Police administration under the leadership of COP Tetteh Yuhuno for improving the fight against crime. The President said there has been an improvement in public safety with reduced highway robberies and unresolved murders. Speaking at the commissioning of an 85-bed ward complex at the Police Hospital in Accra on Tuesday, October 13, President Mahama praised the administration and advised officers to do more to protect lives and property. “This police administration is doing a yeoman’s job, and as Commander-in-Chief and President of the Republic, I want to express the gratitude of our nation to all of you and urge you to keep up the good work,” he said. He reiterated the commitment of the government in resourcing the administration with the right logistics to deliver on its mandate effectively. “It is no wonder everybody wants to visit Ghana, because people say it is the safest country in the whole of West Africa, and I can assure you that we will continue to provide you with the logistics that you need to continue to do your job,” he added. President John Dramani Mahama announced the termination of the Police Hospital expansion contract after 22 years of delays, citing prolonged disagreements with the contractor and cost overruns. He said the government would take responsibility for completing the project, with about GH¢200 million to be provided in the 2027 Budget to bring the expanded facility into service before the end of that year.

items.title: GoldBod tells PAC Bank of Ghana authorised its foreign exchange transactions
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi, says the institution’s foreign exchange transactions are conducted within a market regulated by the Bank of Ghana (BoG), which has provided guidance and authorisation for GoldBod to sell foreign exchange. Speaking before the Public Accounts Committee (PAC), Mr Gyamfi explained that generating foreign exchange for Ghana was one of GoldBod’s primary statutory responsibilities. However, he said the institution needed to sell the foreign exchange it generated to obtain cedis to finance its gold purchases. “First of all, we are set up to generate foreign exchange for Ghana. But in generating foreign exchange for the country, you need to sell that foreign exchange for the country to benefit, so that we can get cedis back to buy gold,” he said. He stressed that the institution’s foreign exchange transactions were subject to the central bank’s regulatory oversight. “We operate within an FX market that is regulated by the Bank of Ghana. The sale of that FX is regulated by the Bank of Ghana,” he told the committee. To explain the regulatory basis for the transactions, Mr Gyamfi said GoldBod formally approached the Bank of Ghana for guidance and authorisation after securing policy approval for its funding model from its supervising minister, the Minister of Finance. He said the approval was obtained under Section 12 of the Gold Board Act before the institution wrote to the central bank on 23 September to seek guidance on its foreign exchange operations. According to him, the request was made in recognition of the Bank of Ghana’s role as the regulator of the foreign exchange market. Mr Gyamfi said the central bank had since responded to GoldBod’s request and provided the necessary guidance and authorisation for the institution to sell foreign exchange. “And I’m happy to inform the committee that the Bank of Ghana has given us that guidance and authorisation,” he said. BoG authorisation recognises GoldBod’s mandate Mr Gyamfi said the Bank of Ghana’s guidance and authorisation recognised GoldBod’s statutory role as a foreign exchange earner. He told the committee that the central bank’s letter expressly acknowledged the institution’s authority to sell foreign exchange. “The authorisation and guidance from the Bank of Ghana recognise Gold Board’s statutory role as a foreign exchange earner,” he said. He added that the letter from the central bank was available for inspection and offered to share a copy with the committee. “The Bank of Ghana made it clear in that letter that the Gold Board is allowed to sell foreign exchange,” he said. Mr Gyamfi maintained that selling foreign exchange was necessary for GoldBod to convert its foreign currency proceeds into cedis to finance gold purchases, while ensuring that its transactions remained within the regulatory framework established by the Bank of Ghana.

items.title: L’IA fait changer d’échelle les menaces cyber
items.description: Selon le Fonds monétaire international, qui s’appuie dans son dernier rapport publié aujourd’hui, mardi 13 octobre, sur des données partielles pour 2026, dans plus de 70 % des cas de vulnérabilités exploitées cette année, les éditeurs de logiciels n’ont presque pas eu le temps de les corriger avant que celles-ci ne soient exploitées par des acteurs malveillants Global Financial Stability Report. Resilience, Risk, and Transformation , FMI, 13 octobre 2026.'> 1 . L’an dernier, ce chiffre se situait à un peu plus de 50 %, selon le FMI. L’organisation attribue la hausse du taux dit « zero-day », soit la part des vulnérabilités exploitées au plus tard le jour de leur divulgation, notamment aux progrès de l’intelligence artificielle. Les modèles d’IA de pointe permettent en effet à des acteurs étatiques, des groupes de ransomware et des employés malveillants de lancer plus d’attaques plus rapidement, et à une plus grande échelle et. al. , Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity in the Financial Sector , Note N26/05, 29 juin 2026.'> 2 . Cette menace fait peser un risque croissant à toutes les échelles : sur les États, les institutions financières et les grandes entreprises, notamment celles qui opèrent dans des domaines stratégiques, mais également sur les particuliers. Selon Comparitech, plus de 2 600 attaques par ransomware ont été revendiquées dans le monde au cours du troisième trimestre 2026, soit 61 % de plus qu’à la même période en 2025 Ransomware roundup : Q3 2026 stats on attacks, ransoms, and active gangs , Comparitech, 7 octobre 2026.'> 3 . CrowdStrike estime que le nombre d’attaques menées par des acteurs malveillants utilisant l’IA a augmenté de 89 % entre 2024 et 2025 2026 Global Threat Report ? Year Of The Evasive Adversary , CrowdStrike, 24 février 2026.'> 4 . L’entreprise de cybersécurité note que l’an dernier, il ne fallait aux cybercriminels que 29 minutes en moyenne pour se propager au sein d’un réseau compromis – contre 98 minutes en 2021. La propagation la plus rapide observée en 2025, quant à elle, n’a nécessité que 27 secondes. L’IA a eu pour conséquence d’abaisser considérablement le seuil d’accès requis pour mener des actions offensives cyber. Les compétences techniques, autrefois nécessaires pour ce genre d’actions, sont aujourd’hui de plus en plus déléguées à un ou plusieurs agents d’IA. La sophistication des modèles leur permet d’opérer avec peu d’instructions détaillées, de pirater de manière autonome des réseaux, de voler des données, et de déployer des ransomwares. L’intelligence artificielle occupe aujourd’hui une place centrale dans le champ de la cybersécurité, tant pour ses capacités offensives que défensives. En juin, les agences de cybersécurité des pays membres des Five Eyes estimaient que les modèles d’IA de pointe devraient, dès les prochains mois, « dépasser les attentes actuelles du secteur, transformant en profondeur les capacités cybernétiques tant offensives que défensives ». L’article L’IA fait changer d’échelle les menaces cyber est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: GCB customers call for more frequent engagement with bank leadership
items.description: Customers of GCB Bank PLC have called for more direct engagement with the Bank’s leadership while sharing feedback on their business needs, growth ambitions and banking experiences during a Customer Town Hall led by Managing Director, Farihan Alhassan. The engagement, held as part of GCB’s Customer Service Month 2026 activities, brought together customers and senior management for an open discussion on service delivery, business growth and ways the Bank can better support customers. Participants shared their experiences, concerns and expectations, while offering suggestions on how GCB could enhance its products, services and customer interactions. A recurring recommendation was for such engagements to be held more frequently and extended to a broader cross-section of customers, underscoring the value customers place on direct access to the Bank’s leadership. The session also highlighted the impact of strong relationship management on customer experience. Several customers took the opportunity to commend their relationship managers for their responsiveness, professionalism and commitment to understanding and supporting their business needs. Speaking at the event, Farihan Alhassan, Managing Director of GCB Bank PLC, reaffirmed the Bank’s commitment to placing customers at the centre of its operations. “Our customers are at the centre of everything we do. Their feedback helps us improve, innovate and serve them better. We value their trust and will continue to listen, learn and go the extra mile to exceed their expectations,” he said. Chief Marketing, Communications and Customer Experience Officer Cynthia Eyram Ofori-Dwumfuo said the Town Hall demonstrated the Bank’s commitment to ensuring customers have a direct voice in shaping their banking experience. “The insights shared by customers are invaluable. They help us understand what matters most to them and guide how we strengthen our services, relationships and overall customer experience,” she said. The Customer Town Hall forms part of GCB’s expanded Customer Service Month celebration, held under the global theme, “The Extra Mile.” For the first time, the Bank has extended its traditional Customer Service Week activities throughout October, creating more opportunities to appreciate customers, gather feedback and reinforce a culture of customer centricity across the organisation. Other activities planned for the month include customer appreciation engagements at branches, customer education sessions, Executive Committee customer interactions, Patrons Appreciation Day and the GCB Aerobics Fiesta. The Town Hall reflects GCB’s commitment to maintaining open dialogue with customers and ensuring their views remain central to the Bank’s efforts to continuously improve service delivery, strengthen relationships and support the growth of the businesses and communities it serves.

items.title: Ratoma : de quoi sont morts les deux occupants retrouvés dans une voiture ? Voici ce que révèle l’autopsie
items.description: Les circonstances du décès de Mamadou Daye Diallo et Kadiatou Keita, retrouvés morts dans un véhicule à Harounaya, dans le quartier de Petit Simbaya, commune de Ratoma, se précisent. Selon les conclusions de l’autopsie, les deux decès sont dus « à une intoxication au monoxyde de carbone. » L’information a été confirmée par le directeur général de la Police technique et scientifique, le colonel Mohamed N’Diaye. D’après ses explications, les examens médico-légaux ont permis de détecter la présence de monoxyde de carbone dans les cœurs des deux victimes. Selon le responsable policier, les deux personnes se seraient installées dans le véhicule pour discuter, alors que le moteur était en marche. Le carburant se serait ensuite épuisé et la batterie déchargée, entraînant une accumulation de ce gaz toxique dans l’habitacle. « Lorsqu’on a procédé à la dissection des cœurs, on y a retrouvé du monoxyde de carbone. C’est donc par intoxication au monoxyde de carbone qu’ils sont morts », a déclaré le colonel Mohamed N’Diaye. Il a également précisé qu’au moment de la découverte du véhicule, celui-ci ne contenait plus de carburant et sa batterie était déchargée. Au regard des résultats de l’autopsie, le directeur général de la Police technique et scientifique a écarté l’hypothèse d’une intervention extérieure dans leur décès. La découverte des deux corps avait suscité de nombreuses interrogations sur les circonstances du drame. Les conclusions de la médecine légale apportent désormais un éclairage sur les causes de leur mort.

items.title: Dark Signals: The death trap of non-functioning traffic lights along Asokwa-Aputuogya Road
items.description: The Asokwa-Aputuogya Road, one of the busiest corridors in the Kumasi Metropolis, has turned into a death trap for motorists and pedestrians due to non-functioning traffic lights along the stretch. A field assessment by JoyNews and Adom News revealed that only 14 out of the 95 traffic lights mounted at eight major intersections along the stretch are functioning. Francis Mensah reports that the non-functioning traffic lights pose a great road safety risk, with the situation already contributing to the loss of 20 lives at some intersections. Crossing any section of the Asokwa-Aputuogya road is one not for the faint-hearted. A sight not missed on the already dark stretch is malfunctioning traffic lights. Anyone crossing the road here could have used the traffic lights for easy passage, but here the pedestrians stand, sticking their necks out to fight for the right of way on the busy stretch. When the contractor completed the dualization of the first phase of the Lake Bosomtwe Road from Asokwa to Aputuogya, they erected 95 traffic lights. But over the years, the poles have failed to serve their purpose. The news team assessed the state of traffic lights along the route. Out of the total, 14 poles have functioning lamps, representing 14.74% functionality, leaving over 85% of the installations non-operational. At six critical intersections, namely Dompoase-Aprabong Junction, Fanko Junction, Agogo Hospital Junction, Atonsu High School Junction, Ahinsan Bonsuom, and Ahinsan Filling Station Junction, all traffic lights mounted on poles were non-functional. Additionally, some of the poles were damaged and had collapsed onto the ground. At Brewery Junction and from the Kumasi City Mall-KFC Junction to the Asokwa Police Station, the situation was slightly better, with some lights working while others remained non-functional. Our assessment revealed not a surprising reality, but a situation which underscores the fatalities recorded on the road. The malfunctioning traffic lights are taking a heavy toll on road safety. The intersections, which are supposed to be controlled, have become free-for-all zones. Commercial drivers, private motorists, motorcyclists and pedestrians all compete for space, leading to severe road hazards, including major vehicle crashes and pedestrian knockdowns. Drivers, residents and traders along the stretch say the situation has persisted for almost a year now. Despite several complaints, the faulty lights have not been repaired, raising questions about maintenance and monitoring by the responsible authorities. Authorities Aware, But No Action Checks by JoyNews reveal that authorities are not unaware of the looming danger. In January 2026, the Asokwa Municipal Chief Executive, together with the Municipal Roads Engineer and the Ashanti Regional Urban Roads team, inspected the Atonsu Market to Ahinsan Bonsuom stretch. It aimed to assess congestion and the state of traffic lights on the Asokwa Interchange–Atonsu corridor. Despite that high-profile inspection, the lights remain dead. On March 23, 2026, the situation worsened when the area experienced a significant traffic jam that left motorists stranded for hours. In a dramatic scene, the Municipal Chief Executive for Asokwa, Amoh Kamel, had to take matters into his own hands, personally directing traffic to ease the heavy congestion on the same stretch. The intervention, while praised by motorists, highlighted the failure of the automated system meant to do exactly that job. Some residents and road users who ply the stretch expressed frustration, saying accidents have increased along the road. “This place is very dangerous. I have personally witnessed many accidents here, involving cars, motorcycles, tricycles and trucks almost every week. Some victims have lost their lives while others sustained injuries,” lamented Fustian Osei, a trader at the Ahinsan Filling Station Junction. “We struggle to cross the road, especially the schoolchildren. Since the traffic lights are not working, drivers and riders do not stop for us. You have to look left, right and centre before crossing, otherwise you could be knocked down,” a pedestrian at Ahinsan Bonsuom said. Drivers who ply the Aputuogya-Asokwa route daily say near-misses and crashes have become common at these junctions, especially at the Dompoase-Aprabong Junction. “There is a slope at the Dompoase-Aprabong Junction and many heavy-duty trucks use this stretch. So, when a truck is descending the slope and gets to the intersection, and vehicles from the other side fail to stop to allow it to pass, it sometimes loses its brakes and rolls backwards, which often leads to accidents,” a driver explained. The Assembly Member for the Atonsu Electoral Area, Francis Asare Sarfo, disclosed that the Oforikrom Municipal Assembly is aware of the non-functioning traffic lights. According to him, the delay in fixing the faulty signals is due to the fact that the road has not yet been officially handed over to the Assembly by the contractor upon completion. Deaths at traffic intersections The role of traffic lights in controlling the flow of vehicles and coordinating pedestrian crossing at intersections is to prevent accidents and reduce congestion. Available data on road crashes in Greater Kumasi from the Building and Road Research Institute of the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR-BRRI) shows that a significant number of accidents occur at intersections. According to the Location Type by Crash Severity report, a total of 408 crashes were recorded at intersections in 2024. A breakdown shows that 20 of the crashes were fatal, 172 victims sustained serious injuries, and 216 escaped the carnage with lacerations. The Deputy Director of the CSIR-BRRI, Prof. Williams Ackaah, says non-functional traffic lights along the Asokwa-Lake Road expose motorists and pedestrians to high risk at intersections. “Look at the number of traffic lights that are not functioning. That’s not good. It means we are not getting the benefits we are supposed to get from the traffic lights. This can result in road crashes and road congestion,” he said The National Road Safety Authority (NRSA) has confirmed that most traffic lights along the corridor are non-functional, highlighting its attendant consequences. According to the Ashanti Regional Director of the Authority, Kwasi Agyenim Boateng, an audit of the road has been conducted and a report on the faulty traffic lights submitted to the Department of Urban Roads. He admitted that any casualties or accidents recorded at intersections where the lights are not functioning should be blamed on the authorities responsible for ensuring the lights are operational. “Most of the traffic lights on that stretch are not working, and as road users, we must acknowledge it. As the road safety authority, we have reported the issue to Urban Roads, which is the responsible agency. Its director has assured us that efforts are underway to get the contractor back on site to fix the lights,” Mr. Boateng admitted Deliberate Turn off? While some link the faulty traffic lights to mechanical failures, others suspect that lights at certain intersections have been deliberately turned off to ease traffic flow and reduce congestion. “We have been informed that some of the non-functional traffic lights were not faulty but were intentionally switched off. According to our sources, this decision was taken because the lights were contributing to heavy vehicular congestion on that stretch, rather than easing traffic flow,” a resident, Adom Helena said The Ashanti Regional Director of Urban Roads, Ing. Naeem Iddrisu, attributed the non-functioning of many traffic lights to mechanical faults but also admitted that some had been deliberately switched off because they were not communicating effectively with the rest of the lights. “Indeed, some traffic lights were deliberately switched off. For instance, the one at the Coca-Cola/Atonsu Market was in good working condition, but it was deactivated around 2003/2004 because it was not synchronizing effectively with the other traffic lights” Prof. Ackaah expressed deep concern over reasons that may account for the deliberate switching off of the lights. According to him, some of the traffic lights along the stretch have improper signal timings which, instead of improving traffic flow, worsen congestion, compelling traffic officers to switch them off for manual control. He warned that regardless of the justification, turning off traffic lights without effective alternative control measures heightens the risk of crashes, particularly for pedestrians and motorcyclists. Contractor yet to hand over road project Assembly Member for the Atonsu Electoral Area, Francis Asare Sarfo explained that until the formal handover is done, maintenance, including repairs of traffic lights, remains the responsibility of the contractor. Mr. Asare Sarfo further revealed that the Municipal Chief Executive (MCE) has held several engagements with both the project consultant and the contractor to ensure the defect is rectified, but the issue persists. Meanwhile, Urban Roads blamed the situation on a combination of factors, including erratic power supply, vandalism, and the theft of cables and other essential components of the traffic lights. Ing. Naeem Iddrisu explained that after the contractor completed construction and moved into the maintenance phase, it was discovered that a significant number of cables from the controllers had been stolen, rendering the lights inoperative. “The challenge has been that after the contractor finished the construction and started the maintenance phase, we realized that many of the cables in the controller had been stolen. We have different types of traffic lights – largely two types. We have solar traffic lights; those don’t need a major controller. But those fed by ECG or the national grid, like the one that was stolen, normally require a controller to regulate them” Prof. Ackaah therefore urged residents and road users to remain vigilant and assist in safeguarding the traffic lights against theft. He further advocated for the deployment of technology to enhance monitoring of the installations. But until the contractor officially hands over the project, how are authorities protecting lives on the road? The MTTD and road safety authority say they deploy officers to intersections where the traffic lights are not working daily. “We have therefore deployed MTTD officers and road safety campaigners to these intersections where the traffic lights are not functioning, and they are there on a daily basis to manage traffic flow and ensure the safety of motorists and pedestrians,” the NRSA director said. But our checks revealed a rather opposite account. From both ends of the road, no officer was sighted on the ground when we visited both at night and during the day. Residents want the traffic light fixed soon The Ashanti Regional Director of Urban Roads, Ing. Naeem Iddrisu, disclosed that arrangements are being made by the government to compensate the contractor for the stolen cables and vandalized components to enable him to return and restore the traffic lights. However, the contractor has yet to agree to the terms and has not provided a definite timeline for completing the repairs. “I have consulted the contractor, and he keeps giving me assurances that he will come, yet he has failed to provide me with a timeline to return to site to fix the traffic lights for us. So, I am still engaging him on the issue.” Road users are calling on the Department of Urban Roads, the Ministry of Roads and Highways and the Asokwa Municipal Assembly to, as a matter of urgency, rehabilitate all faulty traffic signals and put in place a regular maintenance plan for the corridor. From the Kumasi City Mall-KFC Junction to Dompoase-Aprabong Junction, ninety-five poles stand, but 85 percent are without functional bulbs. What is left is the will to fix them. But must it cost lives before authorities fix the lights? Pedestrians and motorists await the red, gold, and green bright colours on the stretch. End

items.title: Les prix du gaz s’envolent en Europe : une bonne nouvelle pour l’Algérie
items.description: Alors que les prix du pétrole s’installent confortablement au-dessus de 100 dollars le baril (105 dollars ce mardi 13 octobre), ceux du gaz flambent aussi et atteignent un niveau jamais vu depuis quatre ans. Il s'agit d’une aubaine pour l'Algérie qui tire l'essentiel de ses recettes en devises des exportations de gaz et de pétrole. Europe : les prix du gaz au plus haut depuis 2022 Sur le marché à terme néerlandais (TTF), référence du marché européen, le prix du mégawattheure (MWh) de gaz naturel a encore progressé ce mardi matin de 2%, atteignant 86 dollars. C'est le plus haut niveau des prix de cette énergie depuis décembre 2022. Depuis le déclenchement de la guerre en Iran, les prix ont presque triplé. Le MWh coûtait 32 euros en février dernier. Les prix du gaz sont portés par plusieurs facteurs : les tensions au Moyen-Orient, un niveau plus bas des stocks européens et l'approche de la saison du froid. Les stocks européens inférieurs aux niveaux habituels Selon le Réseau européen des gestionnaires de réseaux de transport de gaz (ENTSOG), les capacités de stockage de gaz de l'Union européenne étaient remplies au 1er octobre à 72 %. Il s’agit d’un niveau inférieur aux niveaux habituels de pré-hiver, période durant laquelle les pays commencent à puiser dans leurs réserves de gaz pour répondre à la consommation intérieure et à la demande des entreprises. Suivant les explications fournies, les stocks ne constituent pas une réserve secondaire, couvrant par exemple 26 % de la consommation européenne de gaz durant l'hiver 2025-2026, ou encore 30 % la saison précédente. L'approche de l'hiver avec des stocks plus faibles contraint donc l’Europe à dépendre davantage des livraisons de GNL qui arriveront au cours des prochains mois. L’Espagne plus sécurisée grâce à l’Algérie L'Algérie, qui est l’un des principaux fournisseurs de gaz à l’Europe grâce aux gazoducs qui l'a relient à l'Italie et à l’Espagne, conforte son statut de partenaire incontournable et fiable pour le Vieux continent. Selon la presse ibérique, l’Espagne aborde l’hiver avec moins de soucis grâce justement aux approvisionnements qui arrivent d'Algérie ainsi que ceux de GNL qui parviennent des États-Unis. L’Algérie a représenté 34,2 % des importations espagnoles de gaz entre janvier et septembre 2026, devançant les États-Unis qui en ont fourni 30,7 %, et la Russie (15,2 %), indique le site infobae.com . Outre la confirmation de son statut d'acteur important de la carte énergétique, l’Algérie devrait voir ses recettes augmenter sensiblement grâce à la forte hausse des prix du pétrole et du gaz sur les marchés internationaux. Une aubaine pour équilibrer son budget, poursuivre le financement des projets d'infrastructures et les efforts de divertissement de l'économie et maintenir la politique sociale de l'État. Les prix actuels sont nettement au-dessus du prix de référence retenu dans le projet de loi de finances pour 2027 qui vient d'être présenté, soit un prix de référence de 60 dollars le baril et un prix de marché de 70 dollars. L’article Les prix du gaz s’envolent en Europe : une bonne nouvelle pour l'Algérie est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: 'We're not giving up': Activist Thunberg joins France student protests
items.description: Thousands of protesters marched through central Paris on Tuesday as part of nationwide demonstrations supporting high school pupils who have been protesting for better classroom conditions, with Swedish activist Greta Thunberg taking part. With just six months to go before elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron, French authorities had been hoping that the protests were easing ahead of half-term holidays starting at the end of this week. But teenagers at high schools called lycees — backed by university students, teachers, unions and the far-left opposition party France Unbowed (LFI) — have said their demands have not been met. French presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon was seen among the crowd of demonstrators in Paris. Outside the Paris city hall, demonstrators — mostly university students — gathered in the early afternoon to the tune of an orchestra playing the The Rebel Fanfare from the Star Wars movies. “I’m expecting a surge of solidarity,” said 20-year-old Patricia, not wishing to give her surname. “We’re not giving up the fight, whether it’s for the high school students who were hit with a harsh crackdown, or for denouncing police violence,” she added, referencing multiple allegations of police brutality against protesters in recent weeks. The education ministry said 214 schools were closed on Tuesday. Most of these were high schools out of the country’s 3,700. University student union l’Union Etudiante reported that 90 per cent of universities had closed nationwide to show support. Thunberg, who became famous as a teen for school strikes to demand action on climate change, stood among pupils demonstrating outside a school in the capital’s largest suburb, Saint-Denis. “Young people are not being included in the conversation. Our future is being robbed away from us,” the 23-year-old told reporters outside the Paul Eluard high school. ‘Country without a future’ French students say they are determined to press their demands for solutions to too many absent teachers, dilapidated buildings, overcrowded class schedules and other grievances. The protests, launched late last month, have seen teenagers pile up dumpsters and security barriers outside hundreds of lycees. Rallies were also underway in other cities on Tuesday. In the western city of Nantes, thousands marched behind a banner reading “Schools without money, a country without a future”. “I think there are a lot of us in France who are still motivated,” 16-year-old Mariolino said. “Those who think the anger will disappear with the holidays just don’t get it.” In the northeastern city of Strasbourg, Adeline Ferier, 42, a middle school French teacher, said she was demonstrating to support her 16-year-old daughter. “I think it’s great that young people are aware of inequalities and are getting involved,” she said. More than 70,000 people took to the streets last Thursday in the last major event of the movement. Protesters hold placards and banners during a demonstration of high-school students in Lyon, southeastern France on October 13, 2026, as part of a nationwide high school mobilisation. — AFP ‘Issues that deserve time’ The demonstrations in recent weeks have mostly been peaceful, but clashes have occasionally broken out with police. More than 6,800 people — largely minors — have been taken into police custody over the course of the protests, according to the justice ministry. Police have opened internal investigations into 24 allegations of brutality against demonstrators. Some 147 teaching staff members have been injured in the protests, the education ministry said. Authorities said fireworks fired through tubes on Monday injured two school workers in Reims, one school worker in a Paris suburb and a police officer outside a school in Marseille. Tuesday’s demonstrations supporting the students were to be followed on Saturday by wider public rallies against the rising cost of living . Macron, speaking to reporters at a car show on Monday, urged restraint from protesters. “These are issues that deserve time, consultations, discussion and respect,” Macron said just months before elections to replace him. This photograph shows a banner which reads as ’Macron, You break scholl! — AFP After last week’s nationwide demonstrations, the government promised that some 3,000 substitute teachers would be deployed in the coming days to replace absent staff at the 114 worst-affected high schools. The education minister said on Tuesday that 35pc had already been assigned. High school students are demanding a 10 billion-euro ($11 billion) boost for lycees.

items.title: Élim CAN 2027 : le Syli national fixé sur sa double confrontation face à l’Érythrée
items.description: Le Syli national de Guinée connaît désormais son programme pour les 3 ᵉ et 4 ᵉ journées des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. Lors de la prochaine fenêtre internationale, prévue en novembre, les hommes de Paulo Duarte affronteront l’Érythrée à deux reprises, avec un premier rendez-vous à Conakry, le 12 novembre 2026. Selon le programme communiqué par la Fédération guinéenne de football (FGF), la Guinée recevra l’Érythrée le jeudi 12 novembre, à partir de 16 h GMT, au stade du 28 Septembre de Conakry. Quatre jours plus tard, soit le lundi 16 novembre, les deux sélections se retrouveront pour la manche retour. Cette fois, l’Érythrée recevra le Syli national au Caire, en Égypte. L’heure du coup d’envoi et le stade devant abriter cette rencontre restent toutefois à déterminer. Ces deux confrontations représentent une occasion importante pour la Guinée de consolider sa position dans le groupe D et de poursuivre sa course à la qualification pour la phase finale de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations 2027. Après deux journées disputées, l’Afrique du Sud occupe la première place du groupe avec 6 points. La Guinée suit à la deuxième position avec 3 points, tandis que le Kenya et l’Érythrée complètent le classement, respectivement avec 1 point chacun. Face à une équipe érythréenne en quête de points, le Syli national devra donc négocier au mieux cette double confrontation pour rester au contact de l’Afrique du Sud et renforcer ses chances de qualification. Sadjo Bah L’article Élim CAN 2027 : le Syli national fixé sur sa double confrontation face à l’Érythrée est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: RDC : Joseph Kabila prend la tête d’un nouveau front politico-militaire
items.description: Un nouveau front politico-militaire vient rebattre les cartes dans l'est de la Republique democratique du Congo. Annonce le 12 octobre a Goma, le Front pour la refondation de la Nation (FRN) est desormais dirige par l'ancien president Joseph Kabila. Cette nouvelle structure succede a l'AFC/M23 et rassemble plusieurs de ses principales figures, dont Corneille Nangaa et Bertrand Bisimwa, nommes vice-presidents, tandis que Sultani Makenga devient chef d'etat-major. Le FRN affirme vouloir « federer et coordonner toutes les forces de resistance » afin de mettre fin au gouvernement actuel, y compris « par la force ». Un rapport du Groupe d'experts de l'ONU evoquait deja, en juin, une possible restructuration du mouvement autour de Joseph Kabila. Un retour qui ne fait pas consensus Le retour de Kabila au premier plan est particulierement sensible. L'ancien president a ete condamne a mort par contumace en septembre 2025 pour trahison et crimes de guerre, notamment en raison de ses liens avec le M23 et le Rwanda. Lui-meme rejette ces accusations et denonce un proces politique. a Kinshasa, les premieres reactions sont tres dures. Germain Kambinga, ancien ministre de l'Industrie et president du mouvement Le Centre, appelle Felix Tshisekedi a organiser une « mobilisation nationale » contre ce qu'il qualifie desormais de « rebellion de Kabila ». Il accuse le nouveau front de vouloir placer la RDC sous la tutelle du Rwanda et estime que l'enjeu depasse la defense du pouvoir actuel pour concerner directement la souverainete nationale. Cette recomposition fragilise encore davantage les mediations en cours. Alors que Washington, Doha et plusieurs organisations africaines tentaient encore d'imposer une feuille de route entre Kinshasa et l'AFC/M23, la transformation de la rebellion en un front dirige par un ancien chef de l'etat donne desormais au conflit une dimension politique beaucoup plus directe.

items.title: Conakry : Légère secousse sismique dans plusieurs quartiers
items.description: ​Une légère secousse sismique s’est fait ressentir ce mardi dans plusieurs zones de la capitale guinéenne, suscitant une vive surprise parmi les riverains. C'est notamment dans les quartiers de Coléah et de Téminètaye que le phénomène a été le plus perceptible, provoquant de courtes vibrations au niveau du sol et des habitations. Bien que la secousse n'ait duré que quelques secondes, elle a suffi à faire réagir les habitants, dont certains sont brièvement sortis de leurs immeubles et sur leurs balcons pour s'assurer de leur sécurité. ​Heureusement, en raison de sa très faible magnitude, aucun dégât matériel majeur ni blessé n'est signalé. L'événement alimente toutefois de nombreuses discussions, rappelant la rareté mais non l'impossibilité de tels phénomènes dans la presqu'île de Kaloum et ses environs. La population a vite repris son cours normal après cet épisode plus impressionnant que dangereux.

Le FMI relève ses projections de croissance pour le Maroc à 4,5 % en 2026
items.description: Le Fonds monétaire international (FMI) prévoit une croissance de l’économie marocaine de 4,5% en 2026 et de 4,2% en 2027, selon les dernières projections de l’institution. L’inflation devrait, pour sa part, s’établir à 0,9% en 2026, avant de s'accélérer à 1,4% en 2027, souligne le FMI dans son rapport « Perspectives économiques mondiales », publié à l’occasion des Assemblées annuelles du FMI et du Groupe de la Banque mondiale, qui se tiennent du 12 au 18 octobre à Bangkok, en Thaïlande. En revanche, le déficit du compte courant devrait se creuser pour atteindre 4,9% du PIB en 2026, avant de revenir à 4,1% en 2027, fait savoir la même source, notant que le taux de chômage devrait, quant à lui, s’établir à 12,2% en 2026, avant de reculer à 11,3% en 2027. À l’échelle de la région Moyen-Orient et Afrique du Nord (MENA), la croissance devrait se contracter de 2% en 2026, avant de rebondir à 7% en 2027. Au niveau mondial, le FMI prévoit une croissance de 3,1% en 2026, puis de 3,4% en 2027. Parallèlement, l’inflation mondiale devrait marquer une pause dans sa trajectoire baissière, pour passer de 4,1% en 2025 à 4,7% en 2026, avant de refluer à 4,1% en 2027. The post Le FMI relève ses projections de croissance pour le Maroc à 4,5 % en 2026 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Breaking: Appeal Court bars UN rapporteurs, Columbia University from SERAP vs DSS case
items.description: The Court of Appeal in Abuja has barred United Nations Special Rapporteurs and Columbia University from participating in the case involving the Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) and the Department of State Services (DSS). The appellate court also reserved judgment in SERAP’s appeal against a N100 million defamation judgment awarded against the organisation by the Federal Capital Territory High Court. A three-member panel presided over by Justice Danlami Senchi reserved judgment on Tuesday after hearing arguments from SERAP’s counsel, Tayo Oyetibo, SAN, and counsel for the first and second respondents, O.S. Kehinde. The appeal challenges the judgment delivered on May 5, 2026, by Justice Yusuf Halilu. Arguing the appeal, Oyetibo contended that the trial court lacked jurisdiction to award damages in favour of Sarah John over a publication allegedly referring to Sarah David. He also questioned how the trial court established the description of a “tall, large, dark-skinned” woman without a photograph, urging the appellate court to allow the appeal. However, Kehinde urged the court to dismiss the appeal, arguing that SERAP had failed to establish that Sarah John and Sarah David were different persons. He further argued that a person could recognise themselves from a publication based on the description provided, even if their name was not expressly mentioned. items.title: 80–90% of gold purchased and exported is now refined in Ghana– Sammy Gyamfi
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi, says between 80 and 90 percent of the gold purchased and exported by the institution is now refined locally before shipment. He said the development was helping Ghana retain more economic value through job creation, refining fees and the use of silver, a by-product of gold refining, to support the country’s fabrication industry. Speaking before the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) on Tuesday, October 13, Mr Gyamfi said GoldBod was on course to meet and potentially exceed its 2025 gold purchase and export targets, while substantially surpassing its foreign exchange generation performance for the year. He said increased local refining was changing Ghana’s approach to adding value to its mineral resources, noting that refining gold locally before export was not the norm before the establishment of GoldBod. “I’m happy to report to this Honourable Committee that, as we speak, about 80 to 90 per cent of the gold we purchase and export is refined here locally,” he said. Mr Gyamfi said the shift was creating employment opportunities for young people, as local refineries operated around the clock to process gold. “That means jobs for the teeming unemployed youth, because these refineries are operating 24/7, employing Ghanaians,” he said. He added that local refining was helping to retain money within the Ghanaian economy, as fees that would otherwise have gone to overseas refining destinations were now being paid to domestic operators. The development, he said, was helping Ghana benefit beyond the extraction and export of raw gold by retaining more of the economic value generated along the gold supply chain. Silver by-products support local industry Mr Gyamfi also highlighted the benefits of retaining silver, a by-product of gold refining, within the country. He said the silver recovered during the refining process was being sold to generate foreign exchange and used to support Ghana’s fabrication industry. According to him, the approach was helping the country derive additional value from its mineral resources while supporting related industrial activities. By refining more gold locally, Ghana can retain the fees associated with processing the metal and benefit from the by-products, rather than allowing those economic opportunities to accrue to foreign markets. Mr Gyamfi described the developments as progress towards strengthening local participation in the gold value chain. “So, so far, much better,” he told the committee.

items.title: PM Shehbaz, EU official discuss Pakistan's efforts to curb migrant smuggling
items.description: ISLAMABAD: European Union Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration Magnus Brunner called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday to discuss strengthening Pakistan-EU cooperation in migration and mobility, one of the eight pillars of the Pakistan-EU Strategic Engagement Plan 2019. Welcoming Commissioner Brunner on his first visit to Pakistan, the prime minister underscored the importance Pakistan attaches to its partnership with the EU, according to a press release by the PM Office. The premier highlighted Pakistan’s sustained efforts to curb irregular migration and combat migrant smuggling and human trafficking through legislative reforms, institutional strengthening, effective enforcement and international cooperation. He reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening cooperation across all pillars of the Pakistan-EU Strategic Engagement Plan. PM Shehbaz emphasised that efforts to address irregular migration should be complemented by practical opportunities for safe, orderly and regular migration. He noted that expanding legal pathways for Pakistani skilled workers and professionals would help meet the labour market needs of European countries while reducing prospective migrants’ vulnerability to smuggling networks. Brunner appreciated the measures taken and cooperation extended by the government of Pakistan, PMO said. He expressed confidence that these efforts would contribute to expanding legal migration pathways and promoting mutually beneficial labour mobility between Pakistan and the European Union. Naqvi, EU commissioner discuss border security Separately, Brunner also met with Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi in Islamabad, where they discussed enhancing cooperation in border security, legal migration and border management. The meeting was followed by delegation-level talks. Brunner appreciated Pakistan’s measures against illegal migration, describing the 64 per cent reduction in illegal migration to Europe resulting from the country’s efforts as commendable. He said the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) had demonstrated professional competence despite limited resources, which was commendable. He added that the decline in illegal migration would pave the way for legal migration. Naqvi said Pakistan had adopted a zero-tolerance policy towards illegal migration. “After a 64 per cent reduction in illegal migration, our next target is its complete elimination,” the interior minister said, describing illegal migration as a serious global issue. The two sides also discussed the promotion of legal migration and enhancing opportunities for skilled workforce between Pakistan and the European Union. Both sides agreed to further strengthen cooperation in immigration, institutional coordination and border management, and to work together on the EU’s Eastern Corridor Initiative to eliminate illegal migration. They also discussed increasing mutual cooperation to enhance the capacity of Pakistan Coast Guards and agreed to increase collaboration to promote border security and legal migration. Brunner assured Pakistan of all possible cooperation in this regard. The meeting was attended by the interior secretary, special and additional interior secretaries, FIA director general, Federal Constabulary inspector general, NCCIA director general, passports director general, Islamabad chief commissioner and other officials. Last month, Naqvi said Pakistan had recorded a 64pc reduction in illegal migration to Europe, describing the achievement as challenging despite limited resources. He said Pakistan’s next target was to eliminate illegal migration completely, stressing the need to expand legal migration opportunities, adopt modern technology and strengthen institutional capacity. In February, Pakistan and three European countries — Italy, Spain and Greece — reached a consensus on promoting legal pathways to “effectively combat illegal migration”. The three countries endorsed Naqvi’s proposal to establish legal pathways as a strategy to combat illegal migration and human smuggling during a conference.

items.title: Man City: Maresca questions critics of Anfield celebrations after 3-0 win
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has questioned criticism of his players’ celebrations after their 3-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, insisting the team had every reason to celebrate the result. According to the BBC, Maresca defended the celebrations at a news conference on Tuesday ahead of Manchester City’s Champions League clash against Paris Saint-Germain, following criticism directed at the club after its guilty verdict over breaches of Premier League financial rules. “We won 3-0 at Anfield; what do you want us to do?” Maresca said. “Even if it was 1-0, it would be exactly the same. We work every day to win games. It’s the only thing that we can think of. The rest is just things from outside that we need to deal with.” City’s victory over Liverpool was their first match since the verdict, which the club has appealed. The celebrations at the final whistle attracted criticism amid the continuing scrutiny of the club’s financial case. Captain Rúben Dias also defended the players’ reaction, saying they should be free to express their emotions after matches. “I very much stand by the manager’s words,” Dias said. “I think we will enjoy it just as much and celebrate however it feels in the moment. It will be a show of how much it means to us.” Dias added that the players remained calm and trusted the club despite the ongoing legal process. Maresca said the situation had been more difficult for Manchester City supporters than for the players and staff, acknowledging the criticism the club’s fans had faced from rival supporters. “Probably it has been more tough for our fans than for the players or for me because it’s more complicated,” he said. “If I am an Arsenal fan or United fan and you are a City fan I say ‘hey, my friend you cheat.’ So it is probably more tough for them, but we were happy inside the changing room. We were very happy celebrating the three points because it is very difficult at Anfield.” Manchester City are preparing to host reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain at the Etihad Stadium, with Maresca describing the fixture as a major test for his side. “We need the perfect performance because they are the best team in Europe,” he said. “They have won the past two Champions Leagues. We need the perfect game but, doing our best, I think we can beat them and be happy at the end.” The post Man City: Maresca questions critics of Anfield celebrations after 3-0 win appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Senate probes Ondo aircraft crash
items.description: …Asks Air Force leadership to provide budgetary provisions for the maintenance of the aircraft By Henry Umoru, Abuja The Senate has begun a probe into the penultimate Monday tragic crash of a Nigerian Air Force (NAF) aircraft in the Igbokoda area of Ilaje Local Government Area, Ondo State, which resulted in the loss of military personnel and other passengers on board. Consequently, the Senate has mandated its Committees on Air Force and that of Aviation to, as a matter of urgency, carry out an oversight visit to the crash site, interface with the Nigerian Air Force NAF authorities, and conduct a holistic audit of the serviceability and airworthiness of aircraft in the presidential and military fleet. Resolutions of the Senate on Tuesday were a sequel to a motion on the tragic crash of Nigerian Airforce Aircraft in Igbokoda, Ondo State, resulting in the loss of 32 lives, sponsored by Senator Osita Ngwu, APC, Enugu West. The upper chamber also urged the Nigerian Air Force and the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) to conduct a thorough, transparent and comprehensive investigation into the immediate and remote causes of the crash and make its findings public. The Senate then directed the leadership of the Nigerian Air Force to make available to it through the relevant Senate committee the budgetary provisions for the maintenance of the aircraft and to establish the amount provided and whether it was sufficient to prevent the incident, as such provisions were made. It also unanimously adopted the additional prayer by Senator Adams Oshiomhole, APC, Edo, and seconded by Senator Titus Zam, APC, Benue North-West. The Upper Chamber has also urged the Federal Government to prioritise funding for regular maintenance and replacement of ageing military aircraft to safeguard lives of the country’s gallant personnel. The Senate observed a one-minute silence in honour of the passengers and crew members who lost their lives in the ill-fated aircraft. The Upper Chamber condoled with the President and Commander-in-Chief, the Chief of Air Staff, the Nigerian Air Force, the Government and the families of the victims of this national tragedy. Earlier in his presentation of the motion, Senator Ngwu said that “the Senate notes that on Monday, 5th October 2026, a Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 aircraft with tail number NGR 931, carrying 25 passengers and 7 crew members, crashed close to the Naval Base in Igbokoda, headquarters of Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State, while on a routine mission from Benin City to Lagos; “Further notes that this crash, involving military personnel and some civilian passengers, is one of the deadliest military aviation accidents in Nigeria in recent years and has intensified scrutiny of flight safety and operational readiness; “Aware that the air traffic controllers lost contact with the aircraft at about 0813 GMT (that is 9:13 am, local time) and all efforts to reach it on radio proved abortive before the wreckage was located following an immediate search and rescue operation by the Nigerian Airforce in collaboration with other relevant authorities; “Recognise that the Nigerian Air Force plays a crucial role in national defence and intelligence; therefore, operational readiness, serviceability and airworthiness of its aircraft are of strategic importance; “Worried that recurring military air crashes have claimed the lives of gallant officers, raising serious concerns about maintenance culture, ageing fleet, operational safety protocols and airworthiness of military aircraft; “Concerned that without a transparent, thorough and independent investigation, lessons will not be learnt to prevent future occurrences.” The post Senate probes Ondo aircraft crash appeared first on Vanguard News .

Dichemso M/A teachers go house-to-house to get absent pupils back to class after strike suspension
items.description: Teachers at Dichemso M/A School in Kumasi have begun visiting the homes of absent pupils to encourage parents to send their children back to school following the suspension of the teachers’ strike. Despite the resumption of classes, pupil attendance remained low on the first day, leaving some classrooms partially empty and raising concerns about the loss of instructional hours. Teachers boycotted the classroom for two weeks, demanding better service conditions. But they now face a different battle after returning to work. In an interview with JoyNews , the Headmistress of Dichemso M/A School, Helena Amponsah, said teachers had made efforts to contact absent pupils, with some responding to the calls while others had yet to return. “In fact, we even went and also sent some of the students to go and call them, and some reported while others did not. We presume that they have not gotten the news or heard the news. So we hope that from tomorrow going they may come to school,” she said. According to the headmistress, all teachers had reported for duty, adding that the school had resumed lessons and organised morning classes to help pupils return to their academic routine. To address the lost contact hours, she said the school plans to introduce additional lessons and extend teaching hours to cover topics missed during the strike. “We are going to definitely make up to them by doing extra classes, morning classes, afternoon classes, and night classes, to make up to them for all the lost lessons and topics,” she said.

items.title: Pakistan make four changes for third T20I as Sri Lanka win toss, elect to bowl first
items.description: Pakistan made four changes to their line-up for the third and final Twenty20 International against Sri Lanka, who won the toss and decided to bat first at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Tuesday. Razaullah, who made his debut in the first T20I was brought back to the XI while spinner Sufyan Moqim, all-rounder Arafat Minhas and batter Abdul Samad were also handed playing time. Seniors Shadab Khan, Saim Ayub, Naseem Shah and Abrar Ahmed were benched. For Sri Lanka, spinner Maheesh Theekshana — who had an outing to forget in the second T20I — was replaced by younsgter Vijayakanth Viyaskanth. The hosts are looking to complete a clean sweep of the three-match series. After winning the opening T20I by four wickets and securing a convincing 82-run victory in the second match, Pakistan have established a commanding position heading into the series finale. The second T20I saw Pakistan deliver an impressive all-round performance with both bat and ball. Young opener Maaz Sadaqat played a crucial role with a brilliant 96 off 51 deliveries, while captain Sahibzada Farhan contributed 73 runs to help Pakistan post a formidable total of 215 for three. The bowlers then maintained control of the contest, restricting Sri Lanka to 133 for seven to seal a comprehensive victory. For Sri Lanka, the third T20I presents an opportunity to bounce back and finish the tour on a positive note. Captain Kusal Mendis and his teammates will be eager to address their shortcomings, particularly with the bat, after struggling to keep pace with Pakistan’s aggressive approach in the previous encounter. Pakistan, meanwhile, will aim to maintain their momentum and use the final fixture to further strengthen their combinations. The performances of the top-order batters, the effectiveness of the bowling attack and the contributions of the all-rounders could once again prove decisive. With the series already secured, Pakistan will enter the contest with confidence, while Sri Lanka will be determined to avoid a whitewash.
