items.title: Meet Dr Hazel and Nhyira: Mother and daughter called to the Ghana Bar
items.description: It was a double celebration for Dr Hazel P. Berrard Amuah and her daughter, Adwuwa Fynna Nhyira Berrard Quayson, as the two joined Ghana’s legal profession on the same day, marking a remarkable milestone in their family’s history. The mother and daughter were among the newly qualified lawyers called to the Ghana Bar on Friday, October 9, becoming Barristers and Solicitors of the Supreme Court of Ghana. Their shared achievement has attracted admiration, particularly as Dr Hazel adds the legal profession to an already extensive career in corporate leadership, human resource management, insurance and business consultancy. For Dr Hazel, the call to the Bar represents another chapter in a professional journey spanning more than 28 years, during which she has held senior executive positions and received several local and international recognitions. She previously served as the first female Chief Executive Officer of Prudential Life Insurance Ghana, a position she held until April 2024. An accomplished business leader and international public speaker, Dr Hazel has worked across 22 countries in West and Central Africa, building expertise in human resource management, organisational development, business strategy and leadership. Her professional accomplishments have earned her numerous honours, including Ghana Woman Professional of the Year in 2018, HR Practitioner of the Year in 2019, Africa HR Personality of the Year in 2020 and the Global Leadership Award in 2021. She has also received recognition for business leadership, corporate social responsibility and her contributions to human capital development. Beyond her corporate achievements, Dr Hazel has an extensive academic and professional background. She holds advanced degrees in business administration, master’s degrees in Bilingual Translation and Organisational Development, and professional qualifications in insurance and executive coaching. She is a chartered insurer, a member of the Chartered Insurance Institute in the United Kingdom and a Henley-certified coach. Her academic and professional interests have also taken her into teaching, having served as visiting faculty at the China Europe International Business School Africa and as an adjunct lecturer at the University of Ghana Business School. Dr Hazel is also an author whose publications include Winning in the Jungle , People Factory , Dolphins Don’t Swim in Lakes , Where Power Lies , Global Passport and 50 Lessons and Blessings . She has additionally contributed to academic publications addressing leadership, performance management and business strategy in developing economies. Outside her professional commitments, she founded People Factory Limited in 2009, a consultancy specialising in leadership, business strategy and human capital development. That same year, she established the Reach Out and Share Foundation, a non-governmental organisation dedicated to supporting less privileged and underserved communities. Her daughter, Nhyira Berrard Quayson, now begins her own journey in the legal profession, sharing with her mother the distinction of having been called to the Bar at the same ceremony. While both have reached the same professional milestone, their admission to the Bar also represents the beginning of separate careers in a profession that demands dedication, integrity and a commitment to justice. For Dr Hazel, who has spent decades building a career across several disciplines, the achievement reinforces the value of continuous learning and the pursuit of new professional opportunities. Their story is also a reminder that education and professional ambition need not be confined to a particular stage of life. What makes the occasion particularly memorable is that mother and daughter can now celebrate not only their individual achievements but also a professional qualification they have attained together. As the two embark on this new chapter, their shared accomplishment stands as an inspiring example of determination, lifelong learning and the special bond between a mother and her daughter.

items.title: US lists Nigeria among 14 countries facing military aid cuts
items.description: The United States has listed Nigeria among 14 countries facing potential cuts to military assistance over the recruitment and use of child soldiers, a designation that could affect defence cooperation, military training and weapons sales. The designation was contained in the US State Department’s 2026 Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Report, published on October 11, which identified Boko Haram and the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) as armed groups continuing to recruit, abduct and use children in Nigeria. The report covers the period from April 1, 2025, to March 31, 2026, and places Nigeria on the Child Soldiers Prevention Act (CSPA) list alongside Afghanistan, Burma, the Central African Republic, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia, Iran, Russia, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Venezuela and Yemen. Under the CSPA, countries on the list may face restrictions on certain forms of US security assistance and the commercial licensing of military equipment, subject to applicable exceptions, a presidential waiver or other provisions under the law. The report stated that the restrictions would take effect from October 1, 2026, and apply throughout the relevant fiscal year unless an exemption or waiver was granted. “The CSPA prohibits assistance to governments that are identified in the list under the following authorities: International Military Education and Training, Foreign Military Financing, Excess Defence Articles, and Peacekeeping Operations, with exceptions for some programs undertaken pursuant to the Peacekeeping Operations authority. “The CSPA also prohibits the issuance of licenses for direct commercial sales of military equipment to such governments,” the report stated. The designation comes amid continued security cooperation between Washington and Abuja, including joint efforts to combat terrorism and other security threats in Nigeria. According to the report, Boko Haram and ISWAP continue to recruit, abduct and use children as young as 12 in various roles, including as cooks, domestic workers, spies, porters, messengers, bodyguards, checkpoint guards, armed combatants and suicide bombers. The groups reportedly operate across Nigeria, Cameroon, Chad and Niger, subjecting children to physical and sexual abuse and forced drug use. “Boko Haram and ISIS-West Africa continue recruiting, abducting, and using—including through force, fraud, and coercion—child soldiers as young as 12 years old as cooks, domestic workers, spies, porters, messengers, bodyguards or guards at checkpoints, ‘morality police,’ armed combatants, and suicide bombers in attacks in Nigeria, Cameroon, Chad, and Niger; these children are subjected to physical and sexual abuse and forced drug use,” the report stated. The report also raised concerns over the abduction and exploitation of women and girls in northern Nigeria, including forced labour, domestic servitude, sexual slavery and forced marriage. It alleged that Boko Haram had kidnapped thousands of women and girls and forced some into marriages, while punishing girls who refused to marry by compelling them to become suicide bombers. Beyond insurgent groups, the report said criminal gangs in southern Nigeria recruit children for forced criminal activities, including kidnappings and robberies, while exploiting some in sex trafficking. It also identified forced labour in agriculture and mining as a concern involving criminal gangs in the north-west. Apart from the child-soldier designation, the report said Nigeria had failed to meet the minimum standards for eliminating trafficking for the 15th consecutive year, although it acknowledged some improvements in government funding and victim support. The US State Department expressed concern over alleged official complicity in trafficking crimes, stating that the Nigerian government did not report investigations, prosecutions or convictions of public officials allegedly involved in such offences during the reporting period. “The government did not report any investigations, prosecutions, or convictions of government employees allegedly complicit in trafficking crimes or provide details or other actions taken against complicit officials from previous years,” the report stated. It added that “corruption and official complicity in trafficking crimes remained significant concerns.” Vanguard News The post US lists Nigeria among 14 countries facing military aid cuts appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Black Star Fashion Week: Can Ghana turn the runway into a tourism attraction?
items.description: Fashion has always been a powerful expression of identity. Through clothing, textiles, colours and craftsmanship, societies tell stories about their history, values and aspirations. Today, fashion is also a tourism asset, capable of attracting visitors, generating international media attention and creating economic opportunities across the creative industries. Ghana’s maiden Black Star Fashion Week (BSFW), announced by the Black Star Experience Secretariat at the Office of the President, presents an opportunity to explore this connection. More importantly, it raises a question about how the country can use fashion, alongside music, food, heritage and the arts, to strengthen its identity as a destination. Scheduled for November 4 and 7, 2026, the initiative will bring together industry engagement in Accra and a fashion showcase at Royal Senchi. With several established fashion events also taking place in the final quarter, Ghana has an opportunity to build a more coordinated fashion tourism proposition. From Accra to Senchi The structure of Black Star Fashion Week is particularly interesting because it goes beyond the conventional fashion show. The first event, the Black Star Fashion Summit, takes place in Accra on November 4. It is designed to bring together designers, fashion entrepreneurs, industry leaders, investors, buyers, manufacturers, policymakers and media professionals for discussions on the business and future of Ghanaian fashion. The programme includes keynote addresses, panel discussions, fireside conversations, masterclasses, industry presentations and practical workshops. The subjects range from entrepreneurship, branding and digital marketing to textile innovation, manufacturing, fashion finance, export readiness, e-commerce, artificial intelligence, sustainability and intellectual property. These are important conversations for an industry seeking to move beyond individual creative talent towards sustainable businesses, stronger manufacturing capacity and international market access. A particularly notable component is the 16-Region Designer Programme, through which emerging designers will interpret their regions using local identity, heritage, materials, craftsmanship and contemporary design. Five designers will be selected, with one advancing to the flagship showcase at Senchi. This creates an opportunity to present Ghana not simply as a country with talented designers, but as a destination with diverse regional cultures and creative traditions. The second event, at Royal Senchi on November 7, shifts the emphasis from industry dialogue to a wider cultural and fashion experience. The Black Star Fashion Show will be accompanied by a Fashion Village featuring designer showcases, retail, textiles, artisan experiences, brand activations, beauty, technology, food and beverage, tourism and lifestyle experiences. Music, dance, craft, storytelling, heritage and visual arts will also contribute to the programme. The event will include recognition of outstanding contributors to the fashion industry, alongside networking and business engagements connecting designers and creative enterprises with potential buyers, investors, manufacturers and retailers. This combination is significant from a tourism perspective. It creates room for visitors to engage with fashion as part of a broader Ghanaian cultural experience, rather than as a runway spectacle alone. The Accra-Senchi format also offers an opportunity to extend the visitor experience beyond the capital. However, that will require deliberate planning. Transport, accommodation, curated excursions and information about nearby attractions must be incorporated into the visitor proposition if the event is to generate wider tourism benefits. The opportunity beyond Black Star Fashion Week Black Star Fashion Week does not enter an empty space. Ghana already has fashion platforms with established audiences, industry relationships and distinctive identities. Glitz Africa Fashion Week, scheduled for November 10 to 13 in Accra, will bring together designers, manufacturers, textile producers, artisans and creative businesses. Its 2026 theme, Sustainable by Design: Shaping Africa’s Fashion Future, places sustainability, manufacturing, entrepreneurship and market access at the centre of its programme. Rhythms on Da Runway returns on November 28, combining fashion, live music and cultural expression. Its theme, UNBOUND, will broaden representation on the runway, including people of different abilities, backgrounds and body types. The programme also creates opportunities for young people to learn from established practitioners and explore careers in the creative industries. Accra Fashion Week, meanwhile, has an established record of bringing Ghanaian and other African designers, models, buyers and international fashion enthusiasts together. Its previous programming has included cultural tours of Accra, illustrating how fashion events can connect visiting industry professionals with the destination itself. These events should be seen as complementary platforms, not competing attractions. Black Star Fashion Week offers a national identity and policy framework, while the established events contribute their own creative communities, commercial relationships and audiences. Turning fashion into destination marketing The challenge is to connect these platforms to a recognisable Ghanaian tourism story. The Black Star Experience Secretariat, Ghana Tourism Authority, Creative Arts Agency and event organisers could develop a coordinated fashion tourism programme that attracts international buyers, fashion journalists, influencers and visitors from the diaspora. This could include fashion-themed itineraries, designer studio visits, textile and craft trails, shopping experiences, cultural excursions and opportunities to meet artisans. Packages could connect the November events, encouraging visitors to stay longer rather than travel in and out for a single show. The 16-region concept also deserves attention beyond the runway. The designers selected for Black Star Fashion Week could become ambassadors for their regions, with their collections providing a starting point for stories about local textiles, traditional craftsmanship, food, festivals and attractions. International promotion should communicate these experiences well ahead of the events, while partnerships with hotels, airlines, tour operators and travel media could help turn interest into bookings. Success must also be measured beyond attendance and publicity. International visitor numbers, length of stay, visitor expenditure, media reach, retail sales and business opportunities for local designers would provide a clearer picture of the tourism and economic impact. Ghana has the creative talent and cultural diversity to make fashion a distinctive part of its destination identity. Black Star Fashion Week provides an opportunity to organise that story around a national platform, while established events can sustain the momentum. The ultimate ambition should not simply be to put Ghanaian designers on the runway. It should be to give the world more reasons to visit Ghana, experience its culture, buy its creations and discover the places and people behind them. That is how fashion can become more than a showcase. It can become a reason to travel.

items.title: Burkina: plus de 55 millions de F CFA de produits frauduleux saisis
items.description: Dans un bilan rendu public, le lundi 12 octobre 2026, la Coordination nationale de lutte contre la fraude (CNLF) fait état de trois opérations menées les 30 septembre et 1er octobre, ayant permis de mettre au jour plusieurs infractions d’une valeur totale de 55 233 000 F CFA. Sur l’axe Ouagadougou-Koupéla, les agents ont découvert 50 sacs de cyanure, représentant 2,5 tonnes de cette substance hautement toxique, ainsi que 15 colis de cigarettes de contrebande. L’ensemble est évalué à 10 950 000 F CFA. À Loumbila, les contrôles ont porté sur 59 000 litres de gasoil subventionné, estimés à 31 683 000 F CFA. Selon la CNLF, ce carburant était destiné à une unité industrielle au lieu d’être distribué dans les stations-service, contrairement à sa destination réglementaire. Dans le quartier de la Patte d’Oie, à Ouagadougou, une troisième intervention a permis de découvrir 267 cartons d’huile lubrifiante contrefaite introduits en contrebande. Leur valeur est estimée à 12 600 000 F CFA. Présentant ces résultats à la presse, le coordonnateur national, le Dr Mohamadi Compaoré, a dénoncé les conséquences de ces pratiques sur les finances publiques, la sécurité des populations et les entreprises en règle. Il a également salué le travail des agents et le rôle des citoyens dans le signalement des circuits frauduleux. La CNLF entend intensifier ses actions et appelle les populations à maintenir leur coopération avec ses services afin de protéger les intérêts de l’État et de préserver l’économie nationale. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Burkina: plus de 55 millions de F CFA de produits frauduleux saisis est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Jeanne Robles, nacionalizada por la ‘ley de nietos’: “Estoy dispuesta a todo para recuperar el voto”
items.description: Jeanne Robles todavía tenía esperanza. La decisión del Tribunal Supremo de suspender cautelarmente el derecho al voto de quienes obtuvieron la nacionalidad española al amparo de la ley de nietos le parecía “un poco absurda”. Pensaba que, ante el adelanto electoral, el alto tribunal podría reconsiderarla. Pero este lunes, a las cinco de la tarde, la esperanza se le vino abajo. El Supremo había decidido mantener la suspensión, pese a la petición de la Abogacía del Estado y la Fiscalía para que diera marcha atrás. “Estoy dispuesta a todo para recuperar el voto”, asegura, aunque reconoce que le preocupa el coste económico del proceso y cuánto tendrá que pagar para personarse ante el alto tribunal. items.title: Violence in response to a woman's refusal to marry 'profound shame' on society's conscience: Supreme Court
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Criticising patriarchal customs and gender-based violence, the Supreme Court (SC) on Tuesday said it was a profound shame on the conscience of any civilised society when a man, having failed to win a woman’s affection, answered her refusal with violence rather than acceptance. “The sole reason he takes her life is to appease his wounded ego, as he was unable to secure her hand and marry her,” regretted Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar in a nine-page judgment he authored. The observation was made by a three-member bench, which also included Justices Salahuddin Panhwar and Ishtiaq Ibrahim. In its judgment, the bench rejected a criminal review petition by Muhammad Kamran, who sought the commutation of his death sentence to life imprisonment. Kamran, who has already served around 15 years of his sentence in the death cell, was convicted for murdering a woman after she and her family rejected his marriage proposal. Dismissing his review plea, the court ruled that a condemned prisoner could not claim, as a matter of right, that him having served 14 or 15 years of his sentence placed him in the same position as a person sentenced to life imprisonment. “The latter entered prison under a sentence of life imprisonment; the former entered it under a sentence of death. The distinction does not lie in the number of years already spent in prison, but in the sentence which the court actually imposed,” the judgment emphasised. Woman’s consent considered irrelevant, regrets SC The court further observed: “Marriage is a mutual, voluntary covenant that necessitates free consent of both parties. But in a variety of patriarchal systems, it is accepted that men have the exclusive right to select, demand and enforce possession over a woman, irrespective of her wishes.” The judgment stated that a woman “challenges the suitor’s perceived ownership when she exercises her fundamental right to say ‘no’”. “Under a patriarchal mindset, this rejection is taken by that man as a blow to his ‘honour’ ( ghairat ), which results in stalking, home invasion, acid violence or femicide,” the judgment added. The judgment also referred to several customs, such as that of ghag , to illustrate the manifestation of this mindset. Ghag (proclamation in Pashto) is an archaic customary practice where a man unilaterally claims a woman as his bride without her or her guardians’ consent. The court observed that historically, ghag was executed by firing gunshots outside the woman’s residence or making a public declaration. “ Ghag acts as an informal seal or taboo intimidating other perspective suitors away, holding a woman’s marital status hostage as if she is a territory, which is now marked by this man,” the judgment said, adding if the woman or her family resisted, the suitor would frequently employ violence to enforce his claim. As a result, a woman may remain unmarried for years, or even decades, solely due to a declaration that was never followed by a legal or religious ceremony, engagement, or marriage, the court said. It added that the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Elimination of Custom of Ghag Act, 2013, had already declared the custom a cognisable, non-bailable and non-compoundable criminal offence. The judgment then referred to the customs of suara , also known as vani or badal-e-sulh , which it said operated differently from ghag , despite the fact that both portrayed situations where the decision to marry a woman was made by others for a purpose that was not in accordance with her own desires nor benefit. Suara involves a girl or young woman from a family that has committed an offence, such as homicide, given in marriage to a man from the victim’s family as a form of compensation through decision made by a jirga , and serves as a substitute for a criminal proceeding or financial compensation, the court observed. The practice was criminalised through Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2004 and further solidified by Prevention of Anti-Women Practices Act, 2011, it noted. Similarly, there was the custom of watta-satta — another example where the setting of marriage was at the cost of the bride’s well being, the judgment said. Watta-satta , which translates to “give-take”, is a “reciprocal marriage that is prevalent in our country involving a brother and sister from one family marrying a sister and brother from another family”, the judgment said. “The common thread that unites all of these customs is that in this male-dominated society having patriarchal customs and traditions, a woman’s assent to her own marriage is considered irrelevant,” the court regretted. It further stated that it is impossible to reconcile this mindset with Islam, which required woman’s free assent as a prerequisite for a valid nikah . Any adult person, either a man or a woman, was equally entitled to decide whether, when and with whom they would marry, the judgment said. That entitlement, the judgment said, was not a concession that her family, tribe or society, as a whole, had granted to her, the judgment emphasised, adding that a woman possessed this privilege in her own right. “There is no excuse for such behaviour, regardless of whether it is committed in the name of honour, custom, injured pride, or emotions.” The judgment further highlighted that Pakistan was party to the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW). Its Article 16 obliged states to ensure that a woman had the same right to freely choose a spouse and to enter into a marriage only with her free and full consent, the court noted. “A domestic custom or such prevalent mindset that nullifies this choice by force cannot be permitted to survive under the guise of local practice,” the judgment said. In the case at hand, the petitioner, who murdered a woman in cold blood, seemed to have “suffered from the mindset which led to beliefs that a woman is a commodity and it was the right of the suitor to have her, with no possibility of refusal because commodities cannot express”, the court held. The court further said that the attempt to present a woman’s lawful refusal as “provocation” or as a mitigating circumstance was a very “absurd ground” for the plea at hand because no individual had the right to deprive another of their life just because of refusing a marriage proposal. Accepting such an argument would constitute judicial endorsement of the notion that a woman’s will was subordinate to a man’s preference, the court declared. The court held that the petitioner had failed to point out any error to justify the SC’s review jurisdiction under Article 188 of the Constitution. “The submissions advanced are, in substance, a request to rearrange and reweigh matters, which this court, sitting in review, cannot undertake,” it said.

items.title: 2027: INEC unveils QR code for PVCs collection in Lagos
items.description: By Olayinka Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, has intensified efforts to ensure that residents who registered for their Permanent Voter Cards, PVCs, get them timely with the launching of a QR code to assist them locate designated collection centres. Briefing newsmen on preparations for the 2027 elections on Tuesday, the Lagos Resident Electoral Commissioner, REC, Professor Ayobami Salami, noted that PVCs for those who registered between January 5 and July 26, 2026 are not available presently. According to him, “PVCs are currently available for persons who registered between August 25, and December, 10 2025 as well as those who registered between 201l and 2022 but have yet to collect their cards.” “PVCs for persons who registered between January 5 and July 26,2026 are not yet available. The collection of their cards will be announced through official channels in due course. “NEC Lagos State Office has also provided a QR code to help voters locate designated PVC collection centres. I encourage eligible voters to collect their cards promptly and safeguard them, as the PVC remains essential for accreditation on Election Day,” he noted. Salami revealed plans by the commission to ensure that vote-buying won’t be tolerated in next year’s election saying “The Commission is strengthening election risk-management measures and collaborating with the EFCC, ICPC, NEIU and Federal Ministry of Justice to address vote buying, illicit campaign financing and other electoral offences. “Engagement with political parties on financial reporting, auditing and campaign finance compliance will be intensified between 28th October28,2026 and 1st January 1,2027. “I appeal to political parties, candidates, and their supporters to conduct their activities peacefully and in accordance with the law. “The increasing spread of misinformation, disinformation, deepfakes and A-generated content poses a serious challenge to public confidence in elections. “I therefore, urge media organisations to verify electoral information through official INEC channels before publication, particularly information concerning electoral procedures, Commission decisions and election results. “Unofficial projections and privately collated figures must not be presented as results formally declared by authorised electoral officials. “The Commission values your partnership in ensuring accurate and responsible reporting. “The Media Accreditation Portal is expected to become operational before the end of October 2026, with further guidelines to be communicated through official channels. “Preparations are equally advancing for the recruitment, training and deployment electoral personnel.” Professor Salami also revealed a planned Mock accreditation and election simulation exercise in November to fully test the readiness of the commission. “Mock accreditation and election simulation exercise is also scheduled for November 2026, to further assess readiness. “Equally important is the logistical preparation required for the elections. Nationwide, personnel and materials will be deployed across 176,846 Polling Units and 8,809 Registration Areas, supported by over 100,000 vehicles and approximately 4,000 boats. “Sensitive materials are expected to reach local government areas 72 hours before Election Day, with deployment to Registration Area Centres and Super Registration Area Centres Completed by 4:00 p.m. on the eve of the election. “In Lagos State, our preparations take account of population density, traffic conditions, riverine communities and other logistical challenges. “Attention is being given to transportation, storage, electoral facilities, personnel deployment and contingency arrangements to ensure that polling units are rowdy to commence activities as scheduled,” he said. Speaking on voter education and accessibility measures, Professor Salami said; “Voter education and inclusive participation also remain our priorities. “Through the VEP 2027 Election Project Plan, the Commission is expanding grassroots engagement, particularly among women, young people and persons with disabilities. “Activities include community meetings, engagements with tertiary institutions, public debates, mobile cinema and collaboration with the National Orientation Agency. “Accessibility measures include Braille materials, EC30 posters, magnifying glasses and sign-language interpretation at State Collation Centres. “In Lagos State, voter education will continue across communities, markets, educational institutions, religious organisations and other relevant platforms. Improvements are also being made to electronic result transmission and management. “Security remains integral to these arrangements. The Nigeria Police Force, as the lead agency, continues to coordinate with other security and intelligence agencies through the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES).” The post 2027: INEC unveils QR code for PVCs collection in Lagos appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Orodara : La caravane « BARKATOUR » d’Orange Burkina Faso enflamme la ville au rythme de la musique
items.description: La ville d'Orodara, chef-lieu de la province du Kénédougou, a vibré du 7 au 9 octobre 2026 au rythme de la caravane « BARKATOUR » de l’opérateur de téléphonie mobile Orange Burkina Faso. Point d’orgue de cette initiative : un géant concert populaire organisé sur le terrain du 4-Août, réunissant plusieurs artistes locaux et des autorités provinciales. À travers cette tournée, les organisateurs entendent renforcer la proximité de l’entreprise avec les populations et faire découvrir les innovations de l’opérateur. Au-delà de son aspect festif, la caravane a offert un cadre d'assistance directe : des agents d'Orange Burkina ont été mobilisés pour guider les usagers dans la prise en main de leurs services numériques. À cette occasion, les clients ont été formés aux nouvelles fonctionnalités de l'application Max it. Des cartes SIM ont également été offertes aux nouveaux abonnés, tandis que des smartphones étaient proposés à des tarifs promotionnels, à l'instar de modèles habituellement vendus à 22 100 F CFA, cédés pour l'événement à 15 000 F CFA. Un concert populaire pour célébrer la musique Le vendredi 9 octobre 2026, l'ambiance est montée d'un cran avec l'organisation d'un concert sur un podium-car. Plusieurs artistes se sont succédé sur scène pour offrir au public des prestations variées et faire étalage de leur talent. Dans une atmosphère festive, ils ont contribué à donner un éclat particulier à cette soirée alliant divertissement, animation culturelle et promotion commerciale. Le podium-car, véritable attraction de l'événement, a servi de cadre à cette rencontre entre les artistes, les populations et les représentants de la marque Orange. À travers la musique et les animations, la caravane entend ainsi toucher un large public et inscrire l'entreprise dans une dynamique de proximité et de convivialité. Les autorités administratives au rendez-vous L'événement a également enregistré la présence de personnalités locales, notamment le directeur provincial de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme du Kénédougou. Sa participation a témoigné de l'intérêt porté par les autorités régionales à cette initiative alliant développement numérique et animation culturelle. Quand divertissement et numérique se rencontrent En associant concert musical et assistance technique aux usagers, la caravane « BARKATOUR » d'Orange Burkina mise sur une approche qui combine divertissement et découverte des services numériques. Pour les populations, l'événement a représenté une occasion de profiter de prestations artistiques tout en bénéficiant de l'accompagnement des agents d'Orange Burkina pour l'utilisation de certains services mobiles. À travers cette initiative, Orange Burkina entend promouvoir la marque et ses services en allant directement à la rencontre des populations du Kénédougou. L’article Orodara : La caravane « BARKATOUR » d’Orange Burkina Faso enflamme la ville au rythme de la musique est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Ghana sends 61 health workers to Grenada under Labour Export Programme
items.description: Ghana has deployed some sixty-one health workers to the Caribbean nation of Grenada under an arrangement with the country. The government of Ghana’s Labour Export Programme seeks to tackle the Caribbean nation’s shortage of skilled healthcare professionals, while seeking job opportunities for Ghanaian health workers. These health workers will serve in different medical facilities under two-year renewable contracts. Ghana’s Chief of Staff, Julius Debrah, charged the workers to be professional and ethical as they serve as ambassadors of Ghana. “Your certificate or your qualification may open the door for you, but your character will determine how long the door will be kept open,” Dr Debrah said. The Minister of Labour, Jobs and Employment, Emmanuel Kwadwo Agyekum, advised them to respect the terms of their contract at all times. “Go and work well, don’t mess up. Try and raise the flag of Ghana. Be professional. Professionalism is key. This is what we expect from you,” he said. The Minister revealed that the government is planning to deploy additional health workers to Germany and other Caribbean nations. The Labour Export Programme seeks to create employment opportunities abroad for Ghanaians and also help recipient nations to tackle their health sector staff shortages.

items.title: Indignation à la carte (Le billet de Ndiol Maka SECK)
items.description: Lorsqu’une femme est victime de violences, l’indignation est souvent immédiate. Les réseaux sociaux s’embrasent. Les communiqués pleuvent. Les appels à la justice se multiplient. À juste raison d’ailleurs. Parce qu’aucune violence faite aux femmes ne doit être banalisée, encore moins passée sous silence. Mais que se passe-t-il lorsque la victime est un homme ? Les voix se font plus discrètes. Les féministes deviennent étonnamment silencieuses. L’affaire Cheikhou Oumar Ndiaye – ce père de famille qui a perdu la vie dans un drame conjugal impliquant son épouse – en est une illustration parfaite. Elle pose une question dérangeante, mais légitime : la compassion serait-elle devenue une affaire de sexe ? En principe, défendre les droits humains, c’est défendre toutes les victimes de violences, sans exception. Parce que la vie d’un homme a autant de valeur que celle d’une femme. De ce fait, les féministes gagneraient à prendre publiquement position sur ce drame. Non pas pour répondre à une quelconque injonction, mais pour rester fidèles aux principes qu’elles revendiquent. La brutalité n’a pas de sexe. La compassion ne devrait pas en avoir non plus. Ou bien faudra-t-il attendre que la prochaine victime corresponde à leurs catégories habituelles pour que l’indignation retrouve toute sa vigueur ? ndiolmaka.seck@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Kindia : le prix élevé des sérums antivenimeux, jusqu’à 80 dollars le flacon, préoccupe l’IRBAG
items.description: Situé à Koba Pastoria, dans la préfecture de Kindia, l’Institut de recherche en biologie appliquée de Guinée (IRBAG) joue un rôle important dans la prise en charge des victimes de morsures de serpents venimeux. Mais le coût des sérums antivenimeux, estimé entre 70 et 80 dollars le flacon, constitue un véritable obstacle pour de nombreuses familles. Face à cette situation, la direction de l’institution lance un appel à la solidarité pour faciliter l’accès aux soins. À l’IRBAG, des victimes de morsures de serpents sont régulièrement accueillies pour bénéficier d’une prise en charge adaptée. Toutefois, le prix des sérums antivenimeux représente une lourde charge financière, particulièrement pour les populations rurales. Selon Mohamed Sahar Traoré, enseignant-chercheur et directeur général de l’IRBAG, l’établissement privilégie l’intérêt des patients, malgré les difficultés d’approvisionnement et les contraintes financières. « C'est un service à la communauté que nous faisons ici, puisqu'on a un centre de prise en charge dédié. Donc, lorsque les gens sont mordus par les serpents, ils arrivent. C'est vrai que les sérums antivenimés, naturellement, ils coûtent très cher, mais nous avons garantissons que généralement, ce n'est pas généralement, l'institution ne réalise aucun intérêt dans le cadre de la prise en charge d'une morsure de serpents. Donc on revend les sérums au prix d'achat et donc les soins, nous ne faisons pas payer les soins. Mais notre souhait serait que ces sérums-là soient accessibles à la population parce que parfois, dire à un paysan, et c'est ce qui fait quand même une saignée financière importante pour l'institution, parce que beaucoup de personnes qui arrivent ne peuvent pas payer même 100 000 francs. Or, c'est une question de sauver une vie humaine en termes éthiques, en termes déontologiques. On est obligé parfois d'y faire face », a-t-il expliqué. Au-delà des difficultés financières des patients, l’approvisionnement en sérums antivenimeux constitue également un défi pour l’institution. Selon son directeur général, les produits utilisés par l’IRBAG ont été testés dans le contexte guinéen et validés cliniquement. Il rend hommage au professeur Cellou Baldé pour son rôle dans les essais de validation. « Les sérums que nous utilisons, c'est un sérum fort heureusement qui a été testé dans notre contexte et donc il a été validé cliniquement en Guinée. Je voudrais rendre d'ailleurs hommage à Professeur Cellou Baldé qui avait piloté les essais de validation de ce sérum antivenimé. Il a été un grand chercheur de cette institution. Alors, Donc, c'est lui qui sert actuellement des sérums polyvalents sur le plan presque mondial. Et d'ailleurs, c'est en tenant compte de ces rapports qui existent entre nous et la firme qui produit ces sérums, qui fait que nous pouvons avoir à un prix concurrentiel ces sérums antivenimeux. Mais oui, on ne peut pas dire qu'on en dispose. C'est beaucoup d'approbation parfois pour avoir un stock tampon, que nous utilisons pour la gestion des cas d'urgence. On ne les ramène pas au niveau de notre établissement. Si quelqu'un essaie de faire un peu une revue des prix on trouve que pour qu'une dose arrive chez nous, il faut environ 70 à 80 dollars. Et donc nous, dès que ça arrive et ça dépend des espèces, il arrive des fois où pour sauver quelqu'un, il faut 6 flacons. Donc, pour multiplier 70 ou 80 dollars par 6, ou parfois il faut 8 flacons. Donc si c'est le cas c'est 6 fois 8 et ce sont les envenimations par morsure de serpent, c'est en fait un problème de santé publique négligé », a-t-il déclaré. Face à ces difficultés, les responsables de l’IRBAG sollicitent l’appui de l’État guinéen, des fondations et des personnes de bonne volonté. L’objectif est de renforcer les stocks de sérums antivenimeux et de permettre à l’établissement d’assurer gratuitement la prise en charge des victimes de morsures de serpents. Extrait de l’interview avec le directeur général de l’IRBAG à lire bientôt sur Mediaguinee.com. Aboubacar Dramé, correspondant régional à Kindia +224 623 08 09 10 L’article Kindia : le prix élevé des sérums antivenimeux, jusqu’à 80 dollars le flacon, préoccupe l’IRBAG est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Maroc-Mauritanie : Les ressorts d’une relation au-delà des changements gouvernementaux
items.description: La reconduction de Mokhtar Ould Djay au poste de premier ministre et le maintien du chef de la diplomatie mauritanienne alimentent les interrogations sur les perspectives de coopération entre Rabat et Nouakchott. Si plusieurs portefeuilles stratégiques ont changé de titulaires, les grandes orientations de la politique étrangère du pays restent, à ce stade, inchangées. La recomposition de l’exécutif mauritanien relance les interrogations sur l’avenir des relations avec le Maroc. Après la démission du gouvernement, vendredi dernier, le président Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani a annoncé, samedi, la formation d’une nouvelle équipe dirigée par Mokhtar Ould Djay, reconduit à son poste de premier ministre. Cette décision intervient alors que Rabat et Nouakchott entretiennent des relations étroitement liées à des enjeux politiques, économiques et sécuritaires, avec une volonté affichée de renforcer leur coopération bilatérale. La nouvelle équipe gouvernementale conserve plusieurs membres du cabinet précédent, tout en renouvelant les titulaires de portefeuilles importants, notamment ceux de la défense, de l’intérieur et de l’énergie. Un élément retient toutefois l’attention : le maintien de Mohamed Salem Ould Merzoug à la tête du ministère des affaires étrangères, de la coopération africaine et des Mauritaniens de l’étranger. Cette continuité permet d’envisager le remaniement sous l’angle de la stabilité de la diplomatie mauritanienne. Elle ne suffit cependant pas, à elle seule, à préjuger des orientations futures de Nouakchott, lesquelles relèvent des institutions de l’État et de sa direction politique. Les relations entre le Maroc et la Mauritanie s’inscrivent dans une histoire commune nourrie de liens sociaux, culturels et spirituels, auxquels s’ajoutent des intérêts économiques et sécuritaires. Leur coopération dans l’espace africain, notamment au Sahel et dans la région saharienne, constitue un autre enjeu majeur. Les échanges universitaires participent également à ce rapprochement : plusieurs responsables et cadres mauritaniens ont été formés dans des établissements d’enseignement supérieur marocains. C’est notamment le cas de Mokhtar Ould Djay, diplômé de l’Institut national de statistique et d’économie appliquée (INSEA) de Rabat. Reste à savoir si la redistribution des responsabilités au sein du gouvernement mauritanien aura une incidence sur le rythme de la coopération avec le royaume, ou si la permanence des principaux axes diplomatiques permettra de préserver la dynamique bilatérale. Une politique étrangère largement déterminée par la présidence Pour Abdallah Zein, écrivain mauritanien et chercheur en sociologie politique installé en Europe, les relations entre Rabat et Nouakchott relèvent d’une logique de stabilité qui les met, dans l’ensemble, à l’abri des changements de gouvernement. L’influence de l’exécutif sur la politique étrangère demeure, selon lui, étroitement liée aux orientations définies par la présidence. Dans une déclaration à Hespress , le chercheur rappelle que le système politique mauritanien confère au chef de l’État un rôle central dans la conduite des relations extérieures. Les remaniements ministériels ne sauraient donc entraîner, à eux seuls, une modification substantielle des rapports avec le Maroc, en l’absence d’un changement dans les grandes orientations politiques du pays. L’évolution récente des relations bilatérales illustre, à ses yeux, cette importance des choix politiques au sommet de l’État. Sous la présidence de Mohamed Ould Abdelaziz, prédécesseur de l’actuel chef de l’État, les relations entre les deux pays avaient connu une période de refroidissement. Abdallah Zein attribue une partie de cette dégradation à des initiatives personnelles ayant contribué à accentuer les tensions. L’arrivée au pouvoir de Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani a ensuite favorisé une amélioration des rapports entre les deux capitales, permettant notamment de développer la coopération économique et sécuritaire. Dans ce contexte, la reconduction de Mokhtar Ould Djay est perçue par le chercheur comme un facteur susceptible de favoriser la poursuite du rapprochement. Considéré par Abdallah Zein comme une personnalité proche du Maroc, le premier ministre présente également un parcours universitaire marqué par sa formation à Rabat. Le chercheur estime que son maintien à la tête du gouvernement pourrait contribuer positivement aux relations bilatérales. Il évoque aussi l’éventualité d’une visite officielle du président mauritanien au Maroc, sans toutefois présenter cette hypothèse comme une décision annoncée. Au-delà de la composition du nouvel exécutif, Abdallah Zein insiste sur le poids de l’histoire et des intérêts partagés. Pour lui, la solidité des relations maroco-mauritaniennes dépend moins des changements de personnes que de la volonté politique de préserver les acquis et d’élargir les domaines de coopération. Des enjeux sécuritaires et économiques communs Une lecture similaire, quoique davantage centrée sur les dimensions stratégiques, est défendue par Lahcen Hamdat, chercheur en relations internationales spécialisé dans la question du Sahara. Interrogé par Hespress , il estime que la formation du nouveau gouvernement dirigé par Mokhtar Ould Djay témoigne d’une volonté de préserver la continuité des relations entre Rabat et Nouakchott, compte tenu de leurs liens historiques et stratégiques et de la diversité de leurs domaines de coopération. Le maintien du premier ministre, diplômé de l’INSEA de Rabat, ainsi que la reconduction de plusieurs responsables, constituent selon lui des indices de cette recherche de continuité. Le parcours universitaire de nombreux cadres mauritaniens dans les établissements marocains représente également, à ses yeux, une dimension humaine et scientifique qui contribue au rapprochement entre les deux pays. Les changements opérés à la tête de certains ministères, en particulier ceux de la défense et de l’intérieur, doivent néanmoins être interprétés avec prudence. Lahcen Hamdat estime qu’ils doivent être replacés dans le contexte politique intérieur mauritanien. Les considérer comme des préparatifs en vue d’une prochaine étape politique relève, en l’absence d’éléments officiels, d’une hypothèse analytique plutôt que d’un fait établi. Il ne voit donc pas, dans ces changements, la preuve d’une inflexion nécessaire de la politique étrangère mauritanienne. Tant que ses orientations générales demeurent stables, les relations avec le Maroc peuvent, selon lui, poursuivre leur trajectoire actuelle. La coopération entre les deux pays dépasse largement la coordination diplomatique. Elle concerne également la sécurité, le développement, les échanges économiques et les relations culturelles et sociales. La stabilité du Sahel et de la région saharienne occupe, à cet égard, une place centrale, ses conséquences sécuritaires affectant aussi bien la Mauritanie et le Maroc que leur environnement régional. Lahcen Hamdat souligne, par ailleurs, que les initiatives marocaines destinées à renforcer les partenariats avec les pays du Sud et à approfondir les relations avec le continent africain pourraient offrir de nouvelles perspectives à Nouakchott. La position géographique de la Mauritanie et ses liens avec les pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest constituent, selon lui, des atouts susceptibles de favoriser cette dynamique. Le développement de ces relations passe notamment par la poursuite des visites officielles et des travaux des commissions mixtes. Ces mécanismes sont jugés essentiels pour consolider la confiance mutuelle, préserver le bon voisinage et élargir les domaines du partenariat. Le Sahara, un dossier qui impose la continuité du dialogue La question du Sahara marocain demeure un élément important de l’environnement diplomatique régional. Sur ce dossier, Lahcen Hamdat rappelle que la Mauritanie maintient une position de neutralité positive. Dans un contexte où les intérêts sécuritaires et régionaux sont étroitement imbriqués, la préservation des canaux de communication et de coordination avec Rabat demeure, selon lui, une composante essentielle des relations bilatérales. Le nouveau gouvernement mauritanien dispose ainsi d’une marge de manœuvre pour poursuivre le développement des relations avec le Maroc dans plusieurs secteurs, de la sécurité au développement, en passant par les échanges économiques et la coordination régionale. La reconduction de Mokhtar Ould Djay et le maintien du chef de la diplomatie offrent des éléments de continuité, mais ne constituent pas, à eux seuls, une garantie de l’évolution future des relations. Celle-ci dépendra aussi de la capacité des deux pays à concrétiser leurs intérêts communs par des projets et des mécanismes de coopération durables. Comme le résume Lahcen Hamdat, « la continuité des relations reste tributaire du renforcement des intérêts communs et de leur traduction en programmes et en initiatives concrètes ». items.title: Central banks should avoid reacting too strongly to headline inflation – IMF
items.description: The International Monetary Fund has urged central banks to avoid reacting too strongly to high-frequency movements in headline inflation, particularly when those movements are driven by volatile energy prices. According to the Fund, they should, however, respond if higher inflation starts feeding into expectations or wage setting or if technology-driven activity starts strengthening pass-through from headline to core inflation. “Where the post-pandemic inflation episode may have weakened confidence in the monetary policy framework, central banks should be quicker to respond to signs of such feedback from inflation to expectations or stronger pass-through. Indeed, not arresting a drift in inflation expectations in response to the current shocks can be costly when shocks of similar nature arrive in the future because it puts the credibility of monetary policy on the line”. The Bretto Woods institution warned that should the adverse demand effects from the war or materialisation of financial risks eventually dominate—weakening growth materially, softening labor markets, and consequently reducing underlying inflationary pressures—scope for monetary policy to pivot toward easing could emerge. “Any such easing should be gradual and data dependent and remain consistent with returning inflation to target”. Central Banks worldwide are engrossed with inflation targeting policy to address rising inflation. This is done by largely reducing money supply in circulation, but increasing the cost of borrowing. The IMF continued that central banks should explain clearly how incoming data alter the balance of risks, what would justify a change in the policy path, and how they are distinguishing between first-round relative price effects and broader inflationary pressures. This it believes can reduce the risk that households, firms, and financial markets will misread conditional policy guidance as unconditional promises. With fiscal costs rising and electoral pressures intensifying in many countries, central banks may face renewed calls to accommodate higher public borrowing or tolerate inflation above target. The Fund advised that ensuring legal and operational independence of central banks and shielding monetary policy from political interference and fiscal dominance are therefore essential.

items.title: Afrique du Sud: le chef adjoint de la police démissionne sur fond de scandale
items.description: Shadrack Sibiya, numéro deux de la police sud-africaine, a démissionné, le lundi 12 octobre 2026, après l’ouverture d’une procédure disciplinaire à son encontre. Le Service de police sud-africain (SAPS) assimile son départ à une «révocation pour faute déshonorante», dans un contexte marqué par plusieurs affaires judiciaires et des soupçons de corruption. Dans un communiqué publié sur le réseau social X et relayé par plusieurs médias, le SAPS a confirmé que l’avocat de Shadrack Sibiya avait transmis sa démission après le lancement de la procédure disciplinaire. Un porte-parole de l’institution a précisé que ses fonctions avaient pris fin avec effet immédiat et que son départ serait considéré comme une «révocation pour faute déshonorante». Suspendu depuis septembre 2025 pour des soupçons d’inconduite, l’ancien haut responsable est actuellement détenu après son arrestation en septembre 2026 dans une affaire présumée de viol et de manipulation à des fins sexuelles impliquant une personne mineure. Il conteste les faits qui lui sont reprochés. L’examen de sa demande de mise en liberté sous caution a été reporté au mardi 13 octobre 2026. Par ailleurs, plusieurs sources indiquent que son nom est apparu à plusieurs reprises lors des auditions d’une commission judiciaire chargée d’examiner la corruption au sein du SAPS et les liens présumés entre certains responsables policiers et le crime organisé. Des témoins ont notamment évoqué des versements d’importantes sommes d’argent liquide et la remise de cadeaux par des personnes soupçonnées d’activités criminelles. Shadrack Sibiya a rejeté ces allégations, niant avoir reçu des avantages illicites ou commis des actes répréhensibles. Son départ intervient alors que les soupçons de corruption continuent d’ébranler les forces de l’ordre sud-africaines. Les procédures en cours devront permettre d’établir les responsabilités dans cette affaire, tandis que l’ancien numéro deux de la police maintient sa position. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Afrique du Sud: le chef adjoint de la police démissionne sur fond de scandale est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Yémen : l’Iran se pose en médiateur face à l’escalade saoudo-houthie
items.description: L'Iran cherche desormais a s'imposer comme mediateur dans l'escalade entre l'Arabie saoudite et les Houthis. Le ministre iranien des Affaires etrangeres, Abbas Araghchi, a appele son homologue saoudien, Faisal ben Farhan, pour lui proposer son aide afin d'ouvrir un dialogue entre Riyad et le mouvement yemenite. Teheran affirme qu'il n'existe « pas de solution militaire » aux crises qui secouent la region. Cette initiative intervient apres plusieurs frappes meurtrieres contre l'Arabie saoudite, notamment l'attaque contre l'aeroport King Khalid de Riyad, qui a fait au moins 13 morts et plus de 300 blesses. En reponse, la coalition saoudienne a intensifie ses operations contre les Houthis au Yemen, tandis que les combats se durcissent autour de Taez et sur la cote de la mer Rouge. Une carte dans les negociations Les Houthis entretiennent depuis des annees des liens militaires et politiques etroits avec Teheran, qui leur a fourni soutien, expertise et technologies. Mais ils disposent egalement d'une autonomie reelle et ne sont pas de simples executants de l'Iran. En proposant sa mediation, Teheran cherche a transformer cette influence en levier diplomatique et a se presenter comme un acteur capable de contenir l'escalade. L'offre intervient egalement alors que l'Iran negocie lui-meme avec les etats-Unis sur le detroit d'Ormuz, les sanctions et son programme nucleaire. Se presenter comme mediateur au Yemen peut ainsi renforcer sa position dans un rapport de force regional beaucoup plus large. Riyad reste pour l'instant prudent. Le communique saoudien confirme l'echange entre les deux ministres mais ne reprend pas publiquement l'offre de mediation iranienne. Pour Teheran, l'enjeu est clair : montrer qu'apres avoir longtemps ete accuse d'alimenter les conflits regionaux, il peut desormais aussi contribuer a leur reglement.

Nasa's Perseverance rover breaks record for off-planet driving on Mars
items.description: Nasa’s robotic Perseverance rover has now driven farther than any other vehicle on the surface of any world other than Earth, racking up 45.2 kilometres since arriving on Mars in 2021, the US space agency said on Tuesday. The car-sized, six-wheeled rover reached the milestone 5-1/2 years into its mission to explore if conditions conducive to microbial life ever existed on Earth’s neighbour. In doing so, it is visiting some of the most ancient terrain ever encountered in the solar system. “Perseverance’s engineering hardware and instruments are in excellent shape with all redundant systems still available,” Steven Lee of Nasa’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California, told Reuters . “A recent assessment of all systems concluded that they are capable of operating well into the 2030s, likely beyond,” added Lee, the project manager for Nasa’s two Mars rovers, Perseverance and Curiosity . Perseverance has exceeded the previous figure of 45km driven on the Martian surface by Nasa’s Opportunity rover from 2004 to 2018. Both also exceeded the driving distances of any lunar rover. Traversing Jezero Crater Perseverance, with its suite of scientific instruments, has focused on the Jezero Crater, a region in the northern hemisphere of Mars believed to have been flooded with water and home to a lake basin billions of years ago. The rover set the milestone in a journey toward an area called Idubi, through the region off the crater’s western rim nicknamed Lac de Charmes. View this post on Instagram Its companion rover, Curiosity, rolls along in the Gale Crater near the Martian equator. Perseverance is showing no signs of slowing down, Lee added. Its mobility system mechanisms are being tested to show it can drive 100 km or more, he said, with the hardware to be tested to the equivalent of 150km to 300km in the effort. Nasa attributed a major role in Perseverance’s success to its self-driving capability, an autonomous navigation system called AutoNav. Lee said 90 per cent of its drives are done autonomously, with no human intervention. “Perseverance takes stereo images of the terrain ahead, generates a 3D software map, and selects the safest path towards a drive goal,” he said. Another key component is the Vision Compute Element, a fast co-processor computer that allows the rover to process images and run its self-driving software very quickly, almost continuously during drives, Lee added. That contrasts with previous rovers, which needed to pause to “think” before each drive segment, he said. “Perseverance builds on the 29-year legacy of our past Mars rovers — Sojourner , Spirit , Opportunity and Curiosity — each incorporating prior lessons and improving our ability to drive on another world,” Lee said. Potential biosignature Lee said the rover’s biggest achievement was almost certainly its discovery, unveiled last year, of a potential biosignature , or possible sign of ancient microbial life. This was found in reddish rock believed to have formed 3.2 billion to 3.8bn years ago in a river channel feeding the lake that once filled Jezero Crater. The Lac de Charmes terrain, Lee said, may yield clues to early planetary geological processes, such as the effects of large meteorite impacts. Jezero Crater was formed by such an impact early in Martian history. Lee cited orbital evidence that some areas of the rim were once hydrothermal systems with warm or hot groundwater. “These areas may once have provided a warm, watery subsurface environment conducive to life,” he added. “Indeed, some palaeontologists hypothesise that life on Earth began in such environments.” The rover’s original mission envisaged just 20km of driving. Nasa recently approved an extension of its mission to explore the crater rim until roughly the end of 2028. The rover’s plutonium-based power system is performing as expected, Lee said, adding it has “many years of useful energy still available”.

items.title: NCDC reports 1,138 lassa fever cases, 268 deaths
items.description: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has reported 1,138 confirmed Lassa fever cases and 268 deaths across 24 states, with the case fatality rate standing at 23.6 per cent. The agency said this in a statement on Monday, citing its Lassa Fever Situation Report for epidemiological weeks 39 and 40, covering Sept. 21 to Oct. 4, 2026. The report showed that the cumulative case fatality rate of 23.6 per cent was higher than the 18.6 per cent recorded during the corresponding period in 2025. According to the report, 24 states have recorded at least one confirmed Lassa fever case across 119 Local Government Areas (LGAs) nationwide. It stated that Bauchi, Ondo, Taraba, Benue and Edo accounted for 88 per cent of all confirmed cases recorded during the reporting period. The NCDC also identified people aged between 21 and 30 years as the predominant age group affected by the disease during the reporting period. The report further indicated that no new healthcare worker was infected with Lassa fever during epidemiological weeks 39 and 40. In week 40, covering Sept. 28 to Oct. 4, the country recorded three new confirmed cases, a decrease from the 13 cases reported in week 39. The three new cases in week 40 were reported in Bauchi and Benue states, according to the situation report. The cumulative figures for week 40 showed that 1,138 confirmed cases and 268 deaths had been recorded, representing a case fatality rate of 23.6 per cent. In week 39, covering Sept. 21 to Sept. 27, the NCDC recorded 13 new confirmed cases, compared with 11 cases reported in week 38. The 13 new cases in week 39 were reported in Ondo State, bringing the cumulative number of confirmed cases to 1,134 and deaths to 267. The case fatality rate for week 39 stood at 23.6 per cent, compared with 18.5 per cent recorded during the corresponding period in 2025. The NCDC’s situation report provides updates on confirmed cases, deaths, affected states and LGAs, as well as the distribution of infections among different age groups. “Lassa fever is an acute viral haemorrhagic illness transmitted primarily through contact with food or household items contaminated by infected rodents’ urine or faeces. “The disease can also spread through contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person, particularly in healthcare settings where appropriate infection prevention and control measures are not observed. “Members of the public are advised to maintain good environmental sanitation, store food in rodent-proof containers and avoid contact with rats to reduce the risk of infection,” it said. (NAN) The post NCDC reports 1,138 lassa fever cases, 268 deaths appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ex-Liverpool defender Carragher settles tax debt to avoid bankruptcy
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Liverpool and England defender Jamie Carragher will not be declared bankrupt after settling an unpaid tax debt to HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC). According to the BBC, an insolvency judge, Nicholas Briggs, dismissed a bankruptcy petition against the 48-year-old at the Insolvency and Companies Court on Tuesday after the tax authority confirmed that the debt had been paid. The petition was issued in August, with HMRC representative Kevin Hassan telling the court in London that Carragher had settled the outstanding bill. No exact amount was disclosed during the hearing, although the debt was previously estimated at between £700,000 and £800,000. Carragher spent his entire professional career at Liverpool and was part of the team that won the UEFA Champions League in 2005. The former defender retired in 2013 after making 737 appearances for the Premier League club. Since retiring from football, Carragher has built a career as a television pundit, regularly appearing on Sky Sports and CBS Sports. items.title: From journalists’ pursuit to protection? Bid to ban jail sentences for publishing gets boost from syndicate, MPs
items.description: Parliamentarians, legal advocates and representatives of the Journalists Syndicate gathered on Saturday at the Cairo syndicate headquarters for an open seminar to discuss practical steps to curb the use of detention against journalists in lawsuits related to the act of publishing. Participants noted that, despite an explicit constitutional protection against the practice, there is a lack of mechanisms to support a change — a situation which prompted the drafting, almost a decade ago, of a law to prevent imprisonment in publishing crimes. In an attempt to activate the dormant draft law, Tagammu Party MP Atef Maghawry told Mada Masr that he began on Monday to gather lawmakers’ support for the bill, telling Mada Masr he will seek to complete the effort over the coming weeks to secure the bill’s presentation in Parliament’s general session. The discussion came on the back of the ongoing detention of six journalists from independent fact-checking platform Matsda2sh, whose arrests earlier this month brought the number of journalists detained in relation to their work to 26. Multiple voices at the seminar highlighted the risks facing both journalists and citizens alike given the expansion of legal grounds for the arrest of journalists over recent years. Among the attendees was the father of cartoonist and translator Ashraf Omar, who spoke of his son’s imprisonment since 2024 for actions that fall within his duties as a journalist and expressing his opinion. Omar, who has been held in remand for nearly two years to date, is currently facing trial on terrorism charges, his father said. A due-date in his trial this week was postponed until December. Omar’s case is a typical instance of what frequently happens to journalists facing prosecution for their work, according to defense lawyer Nabih al-Genady. In most publication-related cases, journalists are not charged with crimes linked to the specifics of content they published, but authorities instead often rely on a range of other laws and statutes that ultimately lead to their imprisonment, said Genady. This “legislative arsenal” constraining the work of journalists has grown over recent years, according to Journalists Syndicate deputy head Mohamed Abdel Hafiz, who pointed to the enactment since 2015 of the counterterrorism and cybercrime laws, both of which have been used on multiple occasions as grounds for prosecution and custodial sentences for publishing acts. Amr Abdel Rahman, the head of the civil freedoms unit at the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, added to these the telecommunications law, which includes an article on the misuse of social media platforms, while Iman Ouf, the Journalists Syndicate Freedoms Committee head, highlighted Law 180/2018 regulating the press and media, in which Article 12 requires journalists to obtain security clearance before filming in public places. It is only journalists who are subject to restrictions prohibiting photography in public spaces, said Ouf, citing the recent lawsuit filed by the Qena Governorate’s sanitation company against a journalist who had photographed a sewage on a local street. She attributed the instance to an “expansion in the understanding of national security,” noting that most measures taken against journalists are justified under the banner of protecting national security — even when the alleged threat is indirect or undefined. The current approach to handling journalists, said Abdel Rahman, stands in stark contrast to the good faith that originally underpinned Article 71 of the 2014 Constitution. The article was designed to protect journalists practicing their profession, and it explicitly prohibits the use of custodial sanctions as punishment for crimes committed by way of publication, except in cases of incitement to violence or discrimination. But Abdel Rahman emphasized that the law is not merely a written text but a matter of application. Issues surrounding publication-related offenses are a battle for everyone, not just journalists, he added. The same point was echoed by multiple attendees, who stressed that weakening the practice of journalism compromises access to information for citizens, as well as for politicians themselves, with former Egyptian Social Democratic Party MP Samira al-Gazzar stressing the difficulty of MPs’ work in light of compromised access to information, even regarding key items of legislation for which they are responsible. She pointed specifically to the law abolishing old rent and the new law on asylum , which were passed while she was a sitting MP. The pursuit of journalists by authorities holds long-term implications for the practice, said lawyer Asmaa Naeem, one of the several lawyers who represented Omnia Sweidan, who was sentenced over a Facebook post describing instances of obstetric abuse. Journalists should be protected from imprisonment in order to pursue their work, said Naeem, stressing that journalists who make errors should correct them, while those publishing correct information are merely fulfilling their role. It was in a bid to offer concrete protections to journalists that the syndicate began in 2014 its effort to draft a law banning imprisonment in publishing cases, said Khaled al-Balshy, the Journalists Syndicate head, who called in via phone to speak at Saturday’s seminar. Though steps were never taken toward the law’s enactment, it was revived in 2024 by the syndicate committee tasked with drafting media legislation. Steps to activate and introduce better legal cover could support a better atmosphere for the practice of journalism, several of the attendees said, with Balshy gesturing to the initiative, spearheaded by Egyptian Social Democratic Party MP Maha Abdel Nasser, for a freedom of information act and Maghawry, likewise, calling for the activation of limits on the widespread use of remand detention in the new Criminal Procedure Code , the enactment of which is now postponed until October, 2027. Maghawry, who pledged at the seminar to rally support for the draft law, told Mada Masr on Tuesday that he had collected during 75 percent of the 60 signatures required to present a bill to Parliament during Monday’s general session at the House of Representatives, without specifying the exact number of signatories so far. He said he would resume his campaign for backing in the coming weeks when the general sessions resume in November. Speaking on Saturday, Balshy acknowledged the limits of the step for new legislation prohibiting incarceration for publication-related offenses. Even if enacted, he said, imprisonment might not cease immediately. But the principle, he said, is that legislation of this kind would serve as a vital instrument for advocacy and legal recourse to defend journalists in need. The post From journalists’ pursuit to protection? Bid to ban jail sentences for publishing gets boost from syndicate, MPs first appeared on Mada Masr .
